note: Abandoned places reported by news outlets and urbex coverage. Most are private property; check recent photos and ask permission.

spots.name: Prairie Lodge Motel

spots.name: Crystal Mill

spots.name: Marble Ski Area lodge skeleton

spots.name: Titan I missile silo complex near Deer Trail

spots.name: Last Chance Motel

spots.name: Roggen abandoned main street

spots.name: Keota ghost town (church, store, water tower)

spots.name: Great Western Sugar Factory (Longmont Sugar Mill)

spots.condition: Closed in 1977 and vacant since. Repeated fires (2016, 2017, 2020, Aug 2024, Mar 2025) destroyed part of the landmark building. Firefighters say it is structurally unstable with hazardous materials; an explorer fell about 20 ft inside in Oct 2025. Newest info: 2025.

spots.name: Former Denver VA Medical Center

spots.name: Zuni Steam Power Plant

verify.security_notes: 2024 Denver Gazette photos show a no-trespassing sign and broken windows. A March 2025 landmark application froze demolition. No guard or arrest reports found. No 2026 outcome found.

spots.name: Valmont School

spots.name: Abandoned US 34 rest area east of Greeley
spots.location: US 34 east of Greeley, near the Dearfield ghost town site
spots.condition: A roadside rest area that 'looks like it's been abandoned for decades', found by a YouTuber looking for Dearfield. Single undated radio-station article; no exact milepost given.
spots.access: unknown; probably state highway right-of-way

spots.name: Tarado Mansion (former Adams Hotel)
spots.location: Arriba, eastern plains (exact address not given in sources)
spots.condition: Radio-station urbex posts describe it as a massive abandoned building that was a boarding house, then a hotel, then a mansion. The posts are undated, probably 2020s.
spots.access: Private property; sources say trespassing is strictly prohibited

verify.security_notes: Radio-station posts (undated) say it is private property and trespassing is strictly prohibited; no specific enforcement reports found.

spots.name: Walker Home Ruins (John Brisben Walker mansion)
spots.location: Mount Falcon Park, about 0.7 mi from the west trailhead, Morrison, Jefferson County
spots.condition: Stone ruin of a craftsman-style chalet that burned after a lightning strike in 1918. A historical marker says the remains are only the foundation, and one source says stone walls with fireplaces on several floors still stand. Info from about 2020-2026.
spots.access: Public Jefferson County Open Space park, free

verify.security_notes: Foundation ruins on a spur trail in Jefferson County Open Space's Mount Falcon Park. Free and open to the public; dogs must be leashed.

spots.name: Allen Ranch abandoned main house
spots.location: Allen Ranch homestead, Tarryall Valley
spots.condition: Park County Local History archive photos (donated 2020) show the abandoned main house, plus a ruined building photographed in 2003.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Park County Historic Landmark at 24001 CR 77 since 2008, inside the Tarryall Rural Historic District. A fishing site lists 'Upper Allen Creek Ranch' as a private fee fishing area. No info found on current condition.

spots.name: Koch Homestead (Adelaide Ranch)
spots.location: Hunter Creek Valley, White River National Forest, Aspen, Pitkin County
spots.condition: Five relatively intact but deteriorating buildings; on the 2023 Most Endangered list. A barn collapsed in the late 1990s. HistoriCorps has since done stabilization work, but the buildings are not reused.
spots.access: U.S. Forest Service land; reached by trail

verify.security_notes: Stabilization completed by Hunter Creek Historical Foundation, White River NF and HistoriCorps; HistoriCorps restoration on nearby Hunter Creek buildings Aug-Sep 2025. No barriers reported; a 2026 search found no Hunter Creek Valley closure.

spots.name: Homestead Meadows
spots.location: Lion Gulch Trailhead on US 36, 8 mi east of Estes Park; 2.5 mi hike up the gulch, near Lyons/Estes Park, Larimer County
spots.condition: Group of 6-8 abandoned homesteads (1889-1923). The Irvin Homestead is the most intact, with several buildings standing; others are reduced to stoves and cellars. National Register listed. Info about 2020.
spots.access: Public, Roosevelt National Forest

verify.security_notes: Public national forest trail. It closed after the 2013 floods and reopened in 2017 per the Colorado Mountain Club. No barriers reported.

spots.name: Atchee
spots.location: Old Uintah Railway grade north of Mack/Grand Junction (Baxter Pass road), Atchee, Garfield County
spots.condition: Fully abandoned. One standing structure (walls of the steam-engine machine and repair shop) plus foundations; a cabin stands along the rail grade nearby. Info about 2015-2020.
spots.access: Private land, dirt roads

verify.security_notes: Blog: all remnants on clearly posted private property; only the machine/repair shop walls stand. Trail guide: Baxter Pass road runs mostly through private property, no camping. Undated.

spots.name: Russell Gulch
spots.location: About 5 mi north of Idaho Springs on Upper Russell Gulch Road, 9,150 ft
spots.condition: Largely abandoned. Brick schoolhouse, mule barn, IOOF hall, some empty commercial buildings and ruins remain; a handful of residents. A disc golf course runs among the ruins.
spots.access: Mixed; some residents; disc golf by reservation

verify.security_notes: The disc golf course is on private property (PDGA: 'Private Property'), by reservation with the owners; MapQuest lists it as closed. A 2022 state enforcement file cites a Jefferson County Sheriff report about mining claims in the area; its content is unknown.

spots.name: Carr
spots.location: I-25 exit 293 north of Fort Collins, about 3 mi east, Carr, Weld County
spots.condition: A few old houses, the schoolhouse, a church and some store fronts (one source says the storefronts are gone). A few year-round residents; mostly abandoned per ghosttowns.com.
spots.access: Reachable by 2WD; buildings presumably private

verify.security_notes: Wikipedia says a few old houses, a church and the schoolhouse remain, with a growing number of year-round residents. Ghosttowns.com calls it mostly abandoned.

spots.name: Buckingham schoolhouse
spots.location: Townsite in NE Weld County (Pawnee Grassland area); schoolhouse on the hill, Buckingham, Weld County
spots.condition: A 2002 prairie fire burned all original buildings except the schoolhouse on the hill. A ghost-town listing says some structures remain. No recent update found.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: A visitor comment (undated) says a few structures remain, including the schoolhouse on a rise.

spots.name: Wild Horse
spots.location: Straddles US 287, Wild Horse, Cheyenne County
spots.condition: Practically a ghost town apart from the post office. Remaining buildings are mostly south of the highway, and the school is still used as a community center.
spots.access: Mixed; some buildings in use

verify.security_notes: Post office still operating; 1912 schoolhouse used as a community building. No security info.

spots.name: Garcia abandoned adobes
spots.location: Old plaza of Garcia at the New Mexico state line, next to Costilla NM
spots.condition: Abandoned adobe homes and businesses with stucco falling off outnumber the occupied ones; remains of adobe plazas. Info from 2019-2020.
spots.access: Occupied town; buildings private

verify.security_notes: Abandoned adobes with crumbling stucco among occupied homes in a still-inhabited community (2019-2020 sources). No security info.

spots.name: Brown's Dance Hall
spots.location: Ramah, about 45 mi east of Colorado Springs on Hwy 24
spots.condition: Listed and photographed in a 2015 list of abandoned buildings. The town itself is still inhabited. No newer status found.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: An undated town guide lists it among the old buildings still on Ramah's Main Street.

spots.name: Skaguay (Skagway) Power Plant
spots.location: Hydroelectric plant in a steep canyon below Skaguay Reservoir. The trailhead is at the reservoir off CO Hwy 81 near Victor, inside Skaguay Reservoir State Wildlife Area. It is a hike of about 9-10 miles round trip with about 1,600 ft of gain.
spots.condition: Built 1899-1901 (one source says 1909). Abandoned after a 1965 flood damaged the pipeline, which was never repaired. The main building still stands with some equipment, and four decaying houses are nearby. Sources are undated, roughly 2013-2020s.
spots.access: Reached by a trail through a state wildlife area. One local outlet warns that trespassers on private property can be prosecuted. There is no cell service.

verify.security_notes: Trail lies within Skaguay Reservoir State Wildlife Area; sources say a CPW license or pass is required for visitors 18+. Remote, poorly maintained trail with no cell service. No trespass reports found.

spots.name: Robertson Flour Mill (Saguache Flour Mill)
spots.location: Water-powered gristmill near Saguache. It is listed on the National Register as the Saguache Flour Mill.
spots.condition: Three-story log building, about 30 ft square, built in 1873. Abandoned since 1925. The National Register nomination (1978 listing) says it is in surprisingly good condition and still holds its roller machinery, though rodents have damaged the leather pulleys and silk screens. No recent status found.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: National Register nomination: mill closed, most machinery still inside. No recent news found.

spots.name: Schneider Brewery (Philip Schneider Brewing Co.)
spots.location: 236 North Convent Street, downtown Trinidad
spots.condition: SAH Archipedia (from a 1997 book) calls it abandoned and neglected after closing around 1960. An undated audio tour says it stands empty. Another source says part of it was used for school district storage. A January 2023 press release announced selective demolition and restoration by the Downtown Trinidad Development Group. Current status unverified, so it may be under rehab.
spots.access: Privately owned (Downtown Trinidad Development Group as of 2023)

verify.security_notes: Undated sources: building stands empty; Tavern Trove says it is used as school-system storage. No 2025 news found.

spots.name: Salida Smokestack (Ohio-Colorado Smelting & Refining Co.)
spots.location: Former smelter site just outside Salida. It is a wayside on the Collegiate Peaks Scenic Byway., near Salida, Chaffee County
spots.condition: The 365-385 ft brick stack was completed in 1917 and is the only remaining standing structure of a smelter that ran 1902-1920. A July 2025 photo shows it still standing and remarkably well preserved.
spots.access: Owned by the Salida Museum Association and viewable from the roadside wayside

verify.security_notes: Salida Museum Association says it fenced the base and posted KEEP OUT signs, but vandalism persists; viewable from the roadside. July 2025 marker photos show it standing.

spots.name: Blistered Horn Mill
spots.location: About 4 miles south of Tincup, off Gunnison County Road 765, about 4 miles north of Cumberland Pass, near Tincup, Gunnison County
spots.condition: Stamp mill built around 1890 by the Brunswick Mining and Milling Co. It is abandoned and partially collapsed (Wikipedia, undated).
spots.access: Roadside along a county road; ownership unknown

verify.security_notes: Wikipedia (undated) describes an abandoned c.1890 stamp mill at 10,938 ft. No security or ownership info.

spots.name: Marble Mill Site (Colorado Yule Marble Co. finishing mill)
spots.location: Marble Mill Site Park, a 25-acre site in the town of Marble along the Crystal River near County Road 3
spots.condition: The finishing mill closed in 1941 and was in ruins by the late 1970s. Some marble walls and crane piers still stand, along with two small outbuildings. It is listed on the National Register.
spots.access: Public park with open access to the ruins. Removing marble or artifacts is illegal.

verify.security_notes: Public town park with stage, court and picnic areas; volunteer restoration; GOCO grant. Removing marble, artifacts or plants is illegal.

spots.name: Paris Mill
spots.location: At about 11,000 ft, three miles west of Alma, near the Sweet Home Mine, near Alma, Park County
spots.condition: Processed gold, silver and lead ore. Closed in 1937 or 1951 (sources differ). Colorado Preservation describes it as currently abandoned. It was on Colorado's Most Endangered Places list in 2004. A 2024 article (The Flume) reports the first site tour in a 20-year rehabilitation effort, so the buildings still stand, are not in operation, and are being stabilized.
spots.access: Private, with a rehabilitation effort under way; tours have been held

verify.security_notes: Mill is under county-run rehabilitation (Phase 8 contract awarded Mar 2025, delivery 12/31/2025). South Park National Heritage Area says it is closed to the public except for scheduled guided tours of about 10 people. No guards or arrests were reported.

spots.name: North London Mill
spots.location: At about 11,400 ft on the Mosquito Pass road (Park County side), near Alma, Park County
spots.condition: Gold mill that ran 1892-1937, photographed by the Park County archive on Oct 13, 2019. The nonprofit North London Mill Preservation, Inc., formed in 2017, is working to rehabilitate the buildings. It is a Park County local landmark.
spots.access: Managed by North London Mill Preservation, Inc.; reached by a 4WD road

verify.security_notes: The nonprofit asks visitors to come only during scheduled events or to email first. Open houses are scheduled for summer 2026 (e.g. Sept 13, 2026). No guard or arrest reports were found.

spots.name: Magnolia Mill
spots.location: Back side of Montgomery Reservoir, a short hike uphill. The reservoir covers the old town of Montgomery, about 13 miles south of Breckenridge, near Hoosier Pass., near Montgomery Reservoir, Park County
spots.condition: Ore mill that is no longer in use. The Park County archive photographed it in October 2019 and tagged it under 'abandoned mines'. The evidence is weak: a visitor review plus archive tags.
spots.access: unknown (Colorado Springs Utilities owns the reservoir land)

verify.security_notes: A visitor guide says a trail on the far side of Montgomery Reservoir gives a view of the mill. Swimming and water contact are banned at the reservoir. Land and access status of the mill not confirmed.

spots.name: Abbott Church
spots.location: On a knoll above a small creek just north of Lindon, southern Washington County, about 100 miles east of Denver. Elevation.maplogs lists it as an Akron-area point of interest., near Lindon / Abbott, Washington County
spots.condition: Wooden church built in 1913 by settler Albert Abbott. Photo captions and listings describe it as standing alone and abandoned in open farmland. The newest dated source is a Rocky Mountain Profiles photo page from June 2020, which calls it a 'lonely place' but does not itself say abandoned. The adjoining 1913 cemetery is reportedly still in use. Abandonment is moderately confirmed.
spots.access: unknown; the cemetery is in active use

verify.security_notes: June 2020 photo shows it standing in farmland; no security info.

spots.name: Las Mesitas Church ruins (San Isidro)
spots.location: Las Mesitas, on the western edge of the San Luis Valley near Antonito. TopoQuest gives about 37.057 N, 106.127 W. One local report says it is about seven miles from Antonito; the coordinates put it west of town. Next to Las Mesitas Catholic Cemetery.
spots.condition: The church was destroyed by fire in 1975 and stands as a roofless stone shell, a popular photography subject. The bell melted in the fire. The sources give no stabilization or ownership details. The newest info is undated Conejos County Citizen coverage and photo blogs.
spots.access: unknown (next to a Catholic cemetery)

verify.security_notes: Roofless shell after 1975 fire, beside the active Las Mesitas Catholic Cemetery; historical marker on the property; Diocese lists a San Isidro Mission there holding Sunday Mass. Ownership not stated.

spots.name: Aspen Grove brick schoolhouse
spots.location: Only the Aspen Grove area, Pitkin County, is given (cogenweb photo page)
spots.condition: The Pitkin County GenWeb photo page describes an abandoned or long-deserted brick schoolhouse. The source is undated, the details are thin, and current condition is unverified.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Only the undated COGenWeb photo page describes it as long-abandoned.

spots.name: Titan I Missile Complex 2C (725-C), south of Elizabeth
spots.location: South of Elizabeth. Listed as Complex 2C by the state and as 725-C (725th Strategic Missile Squadron, Lowry AFB) by The Military Standard. Sources give no exact coordinates.
spots.condition: Decommissioned and missiles removed in 1965. Denver7 says Colorado's Titan sites 'have been sitting abandoned for more than 50 years'. CDPHE lists it among the 6 former Titan I complexes. No current condition report for this site specifically (info up to about 2021-2025).
spots.access: Unknown. The Titan sites passed to various public and private owners. Officials warn they are hazardous, and trespassers at other Titan silos have been cited and rescued.

verify.security_notes: I found no security or enforcement reports for Complex 2C itself. At the nearby Deer Trail Titan site (2B, a different site on private land), the Arapahoe County Sheriff cited teens for trespassing. One teen there fell into the silo and was hurt. A fire-service source says none of Colorado's Titan complexes are open to the public and some have toxic carbon monoxide levels.

spots.name: Titan I Missile Complexes 1A, 1B and 1C, former Lowry Bombing and Gunnery Range
spots.location: Former Lowry Bombing and Gunnery Range, southeast of Denver and east of Aurora. 1B is state site D015, 1C is D044.
spots.condition: Decommissioned in 1965 and described as abandoned underground complexes. CDPHE says the 1A site was closed in Nov 2004 after soil and water cleanup, and that investigations at 1B and 1C are complete. No current interior condition reported.
spots.access: Complex 1A is owned by the City and County of Denver. Ownership of 1B and 1C is not stated in sources. Sources say one Arapahoe County silo is off limits to visitors.

verify.security_notes: CDPHE: 1A is Denver-owned, and an environmental covenant restricts access to the underground complex. Other sources call the sites private property with fall hazards. No site-specific security or arrest reports found. Teens were cited for trespassing at a different silo (Deer Trail).

spots.name: Huerfano County Correctional Center (former CoreCivic prison)
spots.location: Former CoreCivic 752-bed private prison near Walsenburg
spots.condition: Closed in 2010 and briefly proposed for reopening by the state DOC in 2018. Mother Jones (Sept 2025) says it had 'lain dormant for 15 years'. In 2025 ICE named it a possible immigrant detention site, which drew local opposition. Whether it is operating in 2026 is unconfirmed, so it may reopen.
spots.access: Privately owned by CoreCivic. Not public.

verify.security_notes: CoreCivic-owned, dormant since 2010. ICE toured it March 2025; CoreCivic posted detention-officer jobs 'contingent on contract award'; ~100 protested Aug 2025. No signed contract found. No site-security info found.

spots.name: New Raymer Centre Avenue storefronts
spots.location: Centre Avenue, the main street of New Raymer, off CO-14/CO-52 in northeastern Weld County
spots.condition: Colorado Preservation Inc. put Centre Avenue on its 2017 Most Endangered Places list. The listed threat was demolition by neglect, and Friends of New Raymer (formed 2017) was working on it. CBS Denver described a row of about half a dozen small one-story buildings that have survived while vacant. I found no update after 2017.
spots.access: Unknown. The buildings are in a small inhabited town and a nonprofit is involved, so treat them as private property.

verify.security_notes: Listed as Most Endangered (2017) for demolition by neglect, status 'in progress'; Centre Ave buildings vacant since post office moved in 1970s. No security reports found. In an inhabited town; one Centre Ave building has a LoopNet property record.

spots.name: New Raymer abandoned service station
spots.location: New Raymer townsite (exact address not given)
spots.condition: Lifedeathiron's 2015 list of abandoned Colorado buildings includes 'Service Station - New Raymer'. Newest information is 2015.
spots.access: unknown

spots.name: Hereford Community Center (John van Bergen prairie-style colony)
spots.location: Hereford, about 25 miles north of Briggsdale on CO-14, near the Wyoming line
spots.condition: A Colorado Preservation page (undated) says the Community Center is abandoned and threatened with demolition, while the Hereford Inn is now a single-family home. Ghosttowns.com lists a few old buildings and a grain storage bin still standing. A follow-up search found nothing more recent, so its current status is unverified.
spots.access: Unknown. Other colony buildings, such as the schoolhouse at 67300 Circle Dr., are private homes.

spots.name: Teller City
spots.location: Routt National Forest in North Park, southeast of Walden. It has an interpretive loop trail, and the last stretch of road is high-clearance or 4WD., near Rand / Walden, Jackson County
spots.condition: The USFS says remnants of foundations, log cabins and streets remain at the 1870s-80s silver camp. Ghosttowns.com says parts of cabins are still standing. 2024 travel coverage (Travel Lemming, updated June 2024) describes the site the same way. Ghosttowns.com also once reported an indefinite closure because of beetle-kill blowdown (undated).
spots.access: Public National Forest land, generally open mid-April to mid-November. Check with the USFS before going.

verify.security_notes: USFS historic site with interpretive trail; camping prohibited. An undated ghosttowns.com note reported an indefinite beetle-kill closure; another source says trees were cleared in 2013. Check the Parks Ranger District before going.

spots.name: Phippsburg false-front storefronts
spots.location: Row of false-fronted commercial buildings along CO-131, about 7 miles north of Yampa, Phippsburg, Routt County
spots.condition: An undated Lifedeathiron post calls Phippsburg an 'almost ghost town' whose businesses are all long abandoned. Only the Union Pacific switch yard and the post office were still open. The row of abandoned false-front storefronts was photographed along Highway 131.
spots.access: Unknown. The town is still lightly inhabited and the buildings are likely private, so view them from the highway.

verify.security_notes: Only source is an undated blog post. The town is still lightly inhabited, with a post office and UP switch yard.

spots.name: Kinikinik Store
spots.location: Wooden building just off CO-14 in the upper Poudre Canyon, Poudre Canyon (Kinikinik), Larimer County
spots.condition: Townsquare radio articles describe it as a 'now abandoned Larimer County location', a wooden building beside Highway 14 that most travelers pass without noticing. The articles are undated and were probably written in the 2020s.
spots.access: Unknown, probably private. It is visible from CO-14.

verify.security_notes: Local radio articles (undated) say the deteriorating store and guest cabins still stand. Ownership was not found.

spots.name: Saint Mary's Glacier Ski Area (The Slopes at St. Mary's Glacier)
spots.location: St. Mary's Glacier area off Fall River Road above Idaho Springs; 373 acres in 81 parcels, 3 of them the parking area, Alice / St. Mary's, Clear Creek County
spots.condition: Closed for good in 1986. A 2002 revival plan failed. Listed in 2023-2024 for $7M as sold 'with the buildings, old lifts and carved-out ski runs' (T-bar and rope tows, rental shop, a few small cabins). Described as uninhabited in a 2024 report. Newest info 2024; no sale confirmed.
spots.access: private (backcountry skiers still use the surrounding area)

verify.security_notes: Private 373-acre parcel listed for $7M in 2023. The owning LLC was not named, and I found no report of a sale. The 2008 reopening plan caused disputes between locals protecting private land and people seeking public access. The owner once ran a pay parking lot.

spots.name: Ski Idlewild
spots.location: Ski Idlewild parcel in what is now downtown Winter Park; the parcel was annexed into Winter Park, Winter Park (former Hideaway Park), Grand County
spots.condition: Abandoned after it could not pay a $550 tramway inspection fee (operated from 1961, possibly until 1986). Colorado Ski History says the site is abandoned and boarded up, with all lifts and buildings left except the ice rink. The lodge has been broken into several times and the runs are badly overgrown. Wikipedia says the base lodge was closed and used for document storage. Info is old (about 2007, when a developer proposed building on the parcel). No demolition found, but the current state is unconfirmed.
spots.access: private (town / developer parcel)

verify.security_notes: Annexed into Winter Park in 2007. In 2008 it was announced the old lodge buildings would be burned for a road; I could not confirm that happened. A new residential neighborhood (Sojourn at Idlewild) and new builds now exist on Ski Idlewild Rd, and a 14.36-acre development parcel is listed for sale.

spots.name: Hesperus Ski Area
spots.location: About 11 miles west of Durango off US 160; 160 acres leased from the Scott family, Hesperus, La Plata County
spots.condition: Closed since the 2023-24 season after the gearbox on the Bighorn chairlift (installed 1962) failed. It stayed closed in 2024-25 and 2025-26. The lift, day lodge, rental shop and ski-school yurt are still in place but idle. Newest info Sept 2025; no reopening announced. Note it is temporarily closed, not formally abandoned, by owner Mountain Capital Partners (owner of Purgatory).
spots.access: private

verify.security_notes: Owned by Mountain Capital Partners on leased land; closed since the 2023-24 season after the Bighorn lift gearbox failed; stayed closed for 2025-26 with no reopening timeline (Sept 2025). No security info.

spots.name: Ski San Isabel
spots.location: CO 165 near Bigelow Divide, outside Wetmore (San Isabel National Forest area), Wetmore area, Custer County
spots.condition: Beginner area with 2 rope tows, snack bar, rentals and lodge; operated from the 1960s to 1985. A Colorado Central Magazine piece reports that remains of the lodge, rental shop and rope tow are still there. That piece is undated, and other summaries could not confirm the current condition.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Undated article says lodge, rental shop and rope tow remains survive. A real-estate listing for 9071 State Hwy 165, Wetmore, calls itself the former site, indicating private land.

spots.name: O.A. Greager Scout Camp (Miramonte Lake Boy Scout Camp)
spots.location: Lakefront at Miramonte Reservoir (Dan Noble State Wildlife Area), south of Norwood, Norwood area, San Miguel County
spots.condition: Telluride News calls this formerly popular summer camp 'idle' and 'in limbo for a half dozen years'. Locals objected to its abandonment and to the Western Colorado Boy Scout council's failure to refurbish or reopen it. The article is undated (year unknown), and no follow-up on a sale or demolition was found.
spots.access: private (scout property next to the public state wildlife area)

verify.security_notes: Undated Telluride News article calls the camp idle and 'in limbo' for about six years. Next to the Dan Noble SWA, where CPW requires a license for anyone 18+.

spots.name: Jaffa Opera House
spots.location: Main Street, contributing property in the Corazon de Trinidad historic district, downtown Trinidad
spots.condition: Built 1883. Unused for about 20 years. The city began issuing citations in January 2024. A survey found the northwest corner failing, and wildlife had been living inside. Repairs are estimated at about $13M (CPR, April 2025).
spots.access: Owned by the nonprofit Jaffa Opera House Foundation, which is seeking an EPA remediation grant. Private, no public access.

verify.security_notes: Vacant about 20 years; city began issuing code citations Jan 2024; survey says the NW corner is failing (structural hazard). Nonprofit foundation took ownership and is seeking a $1.9M EPA grant (Apr 2025).

spots.name: Golden Nugget Nite Club (former Antonito Opera House)
spots.location: Main Street, Antonito
spots.condition: Opera house built in 1911 and later converted into the Golden Nugget nightclub. A local radio article describes it as boarded up and sitting abandoned on Main Street. The closing date is not given (year of info unknown, probably 2020s).
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Older articles say it sits quietly or abandoned on Main Street. No current ownership or security info.

spots.name: Querida (Bassick City) and Bassick Mine
spots.location: From Silver Cliff, go 5.5 mi east on Hwy 96, then 1.2 mi south on County Road 341, Querida, Custer County
spots.condition: Remains of the Bassick silver mine and mill ruins, a collapsed shaft and a few old homes are still standing. Year of info unknown (Wikipedia and ghost town guides).
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Mining database lists Bassick Mine land ownership as private and says to assume all mines are private; private mining-claim parcels near the townsite have been sold. No security info.

spots.name: Rosita ghost town
spots.location: Rosita townsite, southeast of Westcliffe and Silver Cliff
spots.condition: A few buildings remain 'in various states of ruin'. The post office closed in 1966. At least one old house is privately occupied. Year of info unknown.
spots.access: Mixed private property. Some residences are occupied.

verify.security_notes: Most of the old town is gone; the area is largely developed into semi-rural home sites. No security info.

spots.name: Uptop Ghost Town
spots.location: Old La Veta Pass, on the former D&RG narrow-gauge route west of La Veta, La Veta Pass (near La Veta), Huerfano County
spots.condition: About a dozen buildings still stand, including a well-preserved chapel that is occasionally open. The site was designated a historic ghost town district in 2000. Year of info unknown.
spots.access: Privately run historic site, occasionally open to the public

verify.security_notes: Privately owned historic site; only a few buildings open to the public and the chapel occasionally open. The owners planned a sale in 2021 (current owner unconfirmed). Survived the Spring Creek fire.

spots.name: Chandler coal camp ruins
spots.location: South of SH 115 along Chandler Road, west of Williamsburg and north of Rockvale, near Cañon City, Fremont County
spots.condition: Victor-American company coal town, completely depopulated since about 1942. Many houses were moved to Cañon City. A February 2022 Outdoor Project gallery shows coal mining ruins and remnants of several buildings along a marked trail. That page does not explicitly name Chandler, so check it.
spots.access: Trail access is reported (trail markers, no map at the trailhead). Ownership unknown.

verify.security_notes: Only foundations and ruins reported; no info found on ownership or trespass rules.

spots.name: Tercio coal camp
spots.location: South Fork of the Purgatoire River, west of Trinidad near the New Mexico border, Tercio, Las Animas County
spots.condition: Ghost town and former CF&I coal camp. The mine closed after 1904, and the company store ran until 1949. A Wikipedia photo shows the large former Colorado Supply Company store building still standing, plus a slag pile. Photo year unknown.
spots.access: unknown (likely private ranch land)

verify.security_notes: CPW says the ~25,000-acre Tercio Ranch is private ranch land normally closed to the public (Ranching for Wildlife hunts only). Not confirmed whether the townsite is inside the ranch.

spots.name: Delhi ghost town
spots.location: US 350, about halfway between Trinidad and La Junta, on the old Santa Fe Trail, Delhi, Las Animas County
spots.condition: A boarded-up 'One Stop' general store with an outhouse, deserted homes and cabins, car skeletons and outbuildings, all in 'pretty rough shape'. Sources date from about 2018 to the 2020s.
spots.access: unknown (unincorporated, private parcels; visible from the highway)

verify.security_notes: Cabins, car skeletons and outbuildings in rough shape, plus the former One Stop store (about 2018 sources). No security info.

spots.name: Timpas ghost town
spots.location: US 350 southwest of La Junta, Timpas, Otero County
spots.condition: Mostly abandoned since the post office closed in 1970. The Timpas School is being restored by a recent owner and is about half livable, so it is no longer fully derelict. Year of info unknown (2020s radio article).
spots.access: School is privately owned. Other parcels unknown.

verify.security_notes: A visitor reports the 1916 school is owned by an older man who gave tours and that it is in better shape. Several other buildings are abandoned. Undated.

spots.name: Garcia Schoolhouse
spots.location: Garcia village, near the New Mexico border (exact address not given)
spots.condition: Schoolhouse built in 1913. It later held a library that closed in 1995, and the building has sat empty since. The article says it 'may get new life'. Year of info about the 2020s. This is a separate building from the Garcia adobes already in the app.
spots.access: Trespassing prohibited

verify.security_notes: Vacant since 1995; 2023 Most Endangered listing (demolition by neglect). Centennial School District is considering renovation for school use; grants fund construction drawings (Colorado Sun, Mar 2024).

spots.name: Unnamed ruins near Gardner (possibly Sharpsdale)
spots.location: Against a rocky bluff near the Huerfano River, a few miles west of Gardner. A commenter places Sharpsdale about 4 mi west, at the junction of the Huerfano River and May Creek., near Gardner, Huerfano County
spots.condition: A 2016 blog describes the 'forlorn and tattered remains' of an old settlement of unknown identity.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Only a 2016 blog found; the site's identity is disputed and some structures date to 1960s repairs.

spots.name: Fitzsimons Place apartments (aka Aspen Grove / Bahamas Apartments)
spots.location: 1568 Nome St, just off East Colfax Ave, Aurora, Adams County
spots.condition: The city condemned and closed this 99-unit, 73,000 sq ft complex in August 2024 (one source says 2025). Code enforcement boarded up windows and doors as units emptied. Later reports say nearly all windows are boarded and fencing has been up for more than a year. BusinessDen called it 'vacant Aurora apartments' in April 2026, when a buyer backed out of buying it.
spots.access: Owned by CBZ Management / Nome Partners LLC (New York). Fenced and boarded. The sale is unresolved and ex-tenants are in litigation.

verify.security_notes: Aug 2024: the city condemned it and planned to board it up and fence the whole property, and police turned away people trying to re-enter. April 2026: a buyer backed out over repair costs. Ex-residents sought to block the sale.

spots.name: Former Early College of Arvada campus
spots.location: 4905 W. 60th Ave, Arvada, Jefferson County
spots.condition: The city bought it for $6.3M in 2024, and it has sat vacant since. A plan to use it as a homeless navigation center drew pushback in 2024. A prospective buyer backed out in 2025 because the improvements cost too much. Neighbors have raised concerns about activity at the vacant property. The city estimated $150K-250K a year in upkeep while it stays vacant (2025).
spots.access: Owned by the City of Arvada and back on the market

verify.security_notes: The city bought it for $6.3M in 2024. The buyer's contract was terminated over renovation costs and the property was relisted. No security reports found.

spots.name: Former Esther Peiffer Elementary School
spots.location: 4997 S Miller Way, Littleton, Jefferson County
spots.condition: Closed in 2023 when Jeffco consolidated schools. Reported as 'the building remains empty while waiting for a buyer.' The board declared it surplus in March 2025. No buyer had been reported as of the latest coverage (2025).
spots.access: Owned by Jeffco Public Schools, which says it monitors and maintains the building until sale

verify.security_notes: Closed in 2023 and declared surplus in March 2025. Still empty and waiting for a buyer. No security reports found.

spots.name: Former Martin Plastics building
spots.location: Englewood; the source gives no exact address and says the building sits raised above the road
spots.condition: A 2023 urbex photo blog describes the former Martin Plastics plant as abandoned. The business started at the site in 1955. The blog does not say when it closed.
spots.access: unknown

spots.name: London Motel
spots.location: Englewood, next to a former trailer park; the source gives no exact address
spots.condition: A 2021 urbex blog says the motel was closed and boarded up long before the neighboring trailer park closed in 2017. Nothing newer was found, so check that it is still standing.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: A 2021 blog says the London Motel (3225 S. Santa Fe Dr) was demolished in 2017. Single source, not confirmed by news.

spots.name: Apparently abandoned building at 1525 Joliet St
spots.location: 1525 Joliet St, north Aurora (80010)
spots.condition: The Aurora Sentinel describes it as an apparently abandoned building whose owners the city has been unable to get to deal with it. The article is undated, probably around 2024. County records show a 2,088 sq ft building on a 0.30-acre lot.
spots.access: Privately owned (the owner is unresponsive to the city)

spots.name: Apex ghost town
spots.location: End of Apex Valley Road, a graded dirt road off CO 119 between Black Hawk and Nederland, at about 9,842 ft
spots.condition: A handful of scattered buildings remain, including the hotel (a Gilpin County historic site) and a log cabin with a plaque marking it Gilpin County Historical Landmark No. 1 (photographed 2014). Two fires and heavy snow have destroyed much of the town. A few summer cabins and one year-round resident remain.
spots.access: unknown (summer cabins are privately held; one blog says it is unclear whether a road with abandoned cabins is public or private; the road is open after snowmelt, usually around April)

verify.security_notes: A few privately held summer cabins and one year-round resident are reported. The road is passable in season.

spots.name: Baltimore townsite
spots.location: About a quarter mile off Tolland Road, between Rollinsville and East Portal, near Rollinsville, Gilpin County
spots.condition: Most of the town was abandoned around 1900. Some cabins may have been used as summer cabins into the 1930s-1950s, and the remains of a saloon are visible. Date of the description is unknown.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: An undated blog says the townsite was bought by private interests around 1990 and the access road is chained and posted no trespassing. Very little original remains.

spots.name: East Portal Camp Cabins (Moffat Tunnel)
spots.location: East Portal of the Moffat Tunnel, at the end of Tolland/Rollins Pass road, East Portal (near Rollinsville), Gilpin County
spots.condition: Five worker cabins remain. Tunnel workers' families lived in them until the early 2000s. A 2023 request asked the Gilpin County Historic Preservation Commission to designate them a local landmark. This is a railroad camp, not a mining site.
spots.access: unknown

verify.security_notes: Five cabins remain, owned by Union Pacific's Real Estate Department on US Forest Service land. Named a Gilpin County landmark June 13, 2023. Colorado Preservation listed vandalism as a threat in 2020. Union Pacific and Gilpin County have discussed a county acquisition.

spots.name: Golden Gilpin Mill
spots.location: About 1 mile north of Black Hawk on CO 119, near the Black Hawk end of the old Gilpin Tramway
spots.condition: Described as the only surviving one of Black Hawk's 1880s-1920s mills. It had stopped operating by 1994. A state mining-reclamation (DRMS) document notes problems with the owner's reclamation permit. No current condition report was found.
spots.access: private (has an owner holding a reclamation permit; inside Black Hawk city limits)

verify.security_notes: Holds a state reclamation permit (M1990-041). In 2020 the City of Black Hawk approved a Special Review Use for mining/milling and tourism, and the plan says the structures will remain. Nothing newer than 2020 found.

spots.name: Stanley Mining Company mill
spots.location: About 1 mile west of Idaho Springs along Clear Creek, near US 6 / I-70
spots.condition: A large four-story mill with metal-clad framing and big tailings piles. A 1950 photo describes it in disrepair, and it has since been stabilized. An adventure park planned for the 40-acre site (first phase targeted for 2019) has no confirmed construction; its website said 'Coming Soon'.
spots.access: private (redevelopment site)

verify.security_notes: Mill described as stabilized. The adventure-park plan (first phase targeted 2019, alpine coaster announced for 2020) was never confirmed as opened or cancelled. A ropes course (Colorado Adventure Center) now lists a Stanley Road address; its link to the mill site is unconfirmed.

spots.name: 7:30 Mine Trail ruins
spots.location: 7:30 Mine Road/Trail climbing Republican Mountain above Silver Plume toward Brown Gulch, ending at the Griffin Memorial
spots.condition: Mine ruins, an abandoned cabin and old ore carts along the old mining road. Most mine openings are closed with grates. The roadbed is crumbling and exposed. Date of the information is unclear (recent trail guides).
spots.access: public trail (Clear Creek County trail); the surrounding Dives-Pelican and Seven-Thirty claims are patented private land

verify.security_notes: The trail is a public right of way, but most adjacent land is private and visitors are asked to respect landowners. In 2024 a landowner and Clear Creek County had an access dispute over road work on the trail.

spots.name: Waldorf ghost town and mine
spots.location: Leavenworth Creek Road off Guanella Pass Road (turnoff about 0.7 mi south of Georgetown Reservoir), at about 11,666 ft below McClellan Mountain, near Georgetown, Clear Creek County
spots.condition: A few original buildings and mine structures remain. A 2007 SummitPost visit describes the remains as standing silent and empty. Archive photos also show collapsed buildings.
spots.access: public land (Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forest, Clear Creek Ranger District)

verify.security_notes: Little of the town remains: some mine ruins and a quonset hut. Trail reviews from 2025 say the high-clearance road was open, with creek crossings. No closures found.

spots.name: Conqueror Mine complex / North Empire
spots.location: North Empire Road (Main St north from Empire) to the tailings-pond parking area, then about 1.5 mi up North Empire Creek through four switchbacks
spots.condition: Some small structures and building remains of the Conqueror Mine, plus piles of wood and mining debris. The boarding house burned after 1960; only its stone foundation was left by 1978.
spots.access: unknown; the road is difficult and needs a high-clearance 4x4

verify.security_notes: 4x4 guides describe tailings and building remains along the Bill Moore Lake 4WD road. No security info found.

spots.name: Anglo Saxon mill and mine ruins / Saxon Mountain cabins
spots.location: Saxon Mountain Road: side road about 200 yd east off a switchback about 2 mi up leads to the mill and mine ruins; several abandoned cabins on the right about 1 mi farther, Georgetown / Lawson, Clear Creek County
spots.condition: Ruins of the Anglo Saxon mill and mine, and several abandoned cabins (2012 off-road report).
spots.access: unknown (partly Arapaho National Forest per trail guides)

verify.security_notes: The only source is a 2012 off-road trip report describing the ruins and cabins along the Saxon Mountain trail.

spots.name: Blue Bird Mine complex
spots.location: Caribou Ranch Open Space: about 2 mi from the parking lot via the Switzerland Trail railbed (DeLonde/Blue Bird loop), on a 0.1-mi spur, near Nederland, Boulder County
spots.condition: A preserved collection of mine buildings and debris, including a bunkhouse later used as a boarding house. Boulder County calls it well preserved. Trip reports are from 2010-2025. This is a protected historic site, not a museum.
spots.access: public land (Boulder County Open Space); closed April 1 - June 30 for wildlife

verify.security_notes: Boulder County Open Space. Closed every year April 1 - June 30 for wildlife, confirmed in a closure listing updated Mar 2026. No bikes or dogs.

spots.name: Cardinal Mill
spots.location: About 2 mi west of Nederland above Coon Track Creek, near Nederland, Boulder County
spots.condition: Mill building still standing. It processed gold, silver and tungsten from 1902 to 1942, and the whole building had begun sliding toward the creek. Boulder County bought it in 2003, and it was listed on the National Register in 2011.
spots.access: public owner (Boulder County) but closed to the public for safety reasons

verify.security_notes: Boulder County bought it in 2003, rehabilitated it 2005-2010, and it was listed on the National Register in 2011. A county remediation project went out to bid (undated). One county page calls it newly open to the public (undated), so current access rules are unclear.

spots.name: Hall Valley / Handcart Gulch mining camp
spots.location: Park County Road 60 north from US 285 at Webster; the Hall Valley/Handcart Gulch staging area is about 4.5 mi northwest, toward Webster Pass, near Webster/Grant (Bailey area), Park County
spots.condition: A handful of buildings, including a tumbledown cabin and some ruins. Much of the townsite is covered by Hall Valley Campground. Date of the information is unknown.
spots.access: public land (Pike National Forest)

verify.security_notes: Site has Forest Service campgrounds (Hall Valley, Handcart). No barriers reported.

spots.name: Former Denny's / Bayou Seafood & BBQ
spots.location: 302 N. Academy Blvd. (near The Citadel mall), Colorado Springs, El Paso County
spots.condition: Former Denny's, closed in 2017 when state regulators seized four Colorado Springs Denny's. It later housed Bayou Seafood & BBQ, which also closed. KOAA called it an 'abandoned restaurant' and KKTV a vacant building when it caught fire on Sept. 2, 2025, and a man was found critically injured inside. The fire was contained; I found no follow-up on demolition. Newest info Sept 2025.
spots.access: Private; fire-damaged, possibly unsafe

verify.security_notes: Fire in Sept 2025. Firefighters found a man inside the vacant building in critical condition. Cause under investigation. No demolition reported.

spots.name: Needle's Eye Tunnel (Moffat Road / Rollins Pass)
spots.location: Rollins Pass Road (east side), just below the Continental Divide, on the abandoned Moffat Road 'Hill Route' grade, Rollinsville, Gilpin/Boulder County
spots.condition: Short high-altitude railroad tunnel still standing but closed year-round after a partial collapse/rockfall (1979 or 1990, sources differ) that blocked through travel; line abandoned 1935, rails pulled. Info current to roughly 2021-2025.
spots.access: public land (National Forest); tunnel closed to entry and vehicles

verify.security_notes: Permanently closed since the 1990 rockfall. Trail sites say it is barricaded and there is no legal workaround. The road is open only up to the tunnel.

spots.name: Devil's Slide Trestles (Moffat Road)
spots.location: Rollins Pass Road east side, about 16 mi from Rollinsville, ~11,600 ft, roughly 1,000 ft above Middle Boulder Creek; short hike from parking area
spots.condition: 1905 wooden trestles still standing but decaying, unstable and closed to crossing; viewable from trail on either side (Denver Gazette, July 2025).
spots.access: public land (National Forest); trestles closed

verify.security_notes: The trestles are decaying, unsafe and closed to crossing; they can be viewed from the trail (Denver Gazette, July 2025). The road is closed to vehicles past the Needle's Eye tunnel.

spots.name: Riflesight Notch Trestle and collapsed Tunnel 33
spots.location: Rollins Pass Road (west side), about 7 mi from Winter Park; Riflesight trail (1.73 mi, west side) passes two small 'twin' trestles and ends at collapsed Tunnel No. 33 beneath the trestle
spots.condition: Loop trestle still standing but dilapidated and unpassable; tunnel beneath caved in after closure; twin trestles nearby. Reports 2007-2022, no 2024-specific report.
spots.access: public land (National Forest); seasonal closure Nov 16-Jun 14 noted

verify.security_notes: The trestle is dilapidated, unpassable and too dangerous to cross (Denver Gazette, July 2025). Structure assessments were held Aug 2025. Tunnel 33 is collapsed.

spots.name: Switzerland Trail grade (Colorado & Northwestern / Denver, Boulder & Western)
spots.location: Switzerland Trail county road / OHV route between Sunset, Gold Hill Road and Glacier Lake (Boulder County Rd 93 north section), Sunset / Gold Hill / Ward, Boulder County
spots.condition: Line closed 1919, rails pulled; roadbed survives with rock cuts, trestle ruins and visible embankment rockwork; a townsite building remains at Sunset. 5280 and Boulder Reporting Lab (July 2026) coverage.
spots.access: public land (county road / National Forest); some private inholdings

verify.security_notes: Open dirt rail-trail and OHV route in Roosevelt National Forest; trail guides updated 2026. No closures found.

spots.name: Hagerman Tunnel and Colorado Midland grade (with Douglass City ruins)
spots.location: Colorado Midland Centennial Trail from trailhead on Hagerman Pass Road (past Native/Windsor Lakes turnoff); tunnel at 11,528 ft, Leadville, Lake County
spots.condition: Abandoned 1887 tunnel (bypassed 1893), open at both ends but west end caved in 1943 - do not enter; trail passes trestle remains, snowshed remains, rock cuts and Douglass City worker-camp ruins. Trip reports to 2020-2022.
spots.access: public land (San Isabel/White River National Forest)

verify.security_notes: Public trail. Interpretive signs were replaced in 2025. The state closed the tunnel after the 1943 west-end cave-in, and the trail stops short of entering it.

spots.name: Colorado Midland Railroad Tunnels (Buena Vista)
spots.location: County Road 371 north of Buena Vista along the Arkansas River; Midland grade bike trail (8.8 mi) from River Park/Shields Gulch
spots.condition: Rock tunnels from the Colorado Midland (abandoned c.1918-1922) still standing; can be driven, biked or walked through; trestles scrapped in WWII. Info to roughly 2021-2024.
spots.access: public (county road / BLM)

verify.security_notes: Tunnels on public County Road 371, open with no fees; a visitor guide says no fences or warning signs. Chaffee County did structural testing and stabilization planning (c. 2022), with temporary road closures. Land along the route is USFS/BLM with some private parcels.

spots.name: Colorado Midland tunnels in Ute Pass
spots.location: Old Colorado Midland grade up Ute Pass above US 24 (Ute Pass trail; Tunnel 2 just past hike-a-bike section), Manitou Springs / Cascade, El Paso County
spots.condition: Several 1886 Colorado Midland tunnels (5-8 per sources) remain on the abandoned grade, last Midland Terminal train 1949; some may be on restricted property. Undated/older sources.
spots.access: mixed public/private - check land status

verify.security_notes: Trail guides say a fence inside the 4th tunnel marks where private land begins. A local radio article warns entry risks bodily harm and trespassing prosecution. Rockfall is reported in the tunnels. Sources are undated.

spots.name: Alpine Tunnel West Portal and Alpine Station
spots.location: End of FS Roads 765/839, about 13 mi northeast of Pitkin
spots.condition: DSP&P tunnel abandoned 1910; west portal buried by landslides with rails/redwood timbers inside; ruins of engine house and section house, part of turntable; telegraph office/platform partly restored by volunteers. Road damaged 2016, briefly reopened Aug 2022; check status.
spots.access: public land (Gunnison National Forest)

verify.security_notes: 2024: Forest Service reopened Alpine Tunnel Road (NFSR 839) after Palisade Wall rebuild and reversed the closure order for the historic district. A boulder blocked the West Portal parking area, so visitors were told to hike the last mile. An undated Denver Gazette note says the west side is closed to vehicles after an avalanche; I could not confirm when. No guards or citations found.

spots.name: Boreas Pass railroad relics (Baker's Tank, engine house ruins)
spots.location: Boreas Pass Road (DSP&P/C&S grade); Baker's Tank at MP 102.16 ~3-4 mi below summit on Breckenridge side; engine house ruins across road from summit section house, Breckenridge / Como, Summit-Park County
spots.condition: Last train 1937; wooden Baker's water tank still stands (restored 1958); foundations/remains of 1883 engine house (burned 1909) visible at summit; summit section house is a restored hut.
spots.access: public land (National Forest road)

verify.security_notes: National Forest road and trailhead, used by hikers in 2025. A 2025 blog says the engine house ruins are still visible. The section house is a hut run by Summit Huts and the Forest Service.

spots.name: Sargents D&RGW Water Tank
spots.location: Beside former Marshall Pass line bed in Sargents, east of Monarch Pass on US 50
spots.condition: 1937 redwood 55,500-gal tank still standing ~12 ft from the former tracks (removed 1955); only surviving tank in original location on the Marshall Pass route; acquired 2005 by local historical association.
spots.access: private (historical association), visible from public road

verify.security_notes: Bought in 2005 by the Upper Tomichi Historical & Community Association for preservation. Restoration donations are taken at the site (2009 article). No security info found.

spots.name: Trout Lake Rio Grande Southern Water Tank and Trestle (Bridge 51-A)
spots.location: Galloping Goose Trail around Trout Lake; trestle at east end of lake (Trestle Road), Trout Lake / Telluride, San Miguel County
spots.condition: RGS abandoned c.1951-1953; 50,000-gal wooden water tank (NRHP 2003) and wooden trestle still standing; trestle stabilized by Forest Service, closed to vehicles.
spots.access: public land (Uncompahgre National Forest) / trail

verify.security_notes: Trestle is preserved and closed to vehicles. Forest Service put a foundation under the tank to stabilize it (undated). Reached by a public gravel trail (2026 TrailLink guide). No guards or enforcement reported.

spots.name: Rattlesnake Trestle (San Luis Southern Railway)
spots.location: Near Blanca along County Road 12 (old road crossing, bypassed by newer bridge)
spots.condition: 1910 wooden trestle, 190 ft long, still standing after line closure; used as a county road bridge until replaced; NRHP 2004.
spots.access: unknown (county ROW)

verify.security_notes: Sources only cover history and the 2004 NRHP listing (Costilla County, near Smith Reservoir outlet). No current condition or security info found.

spots.name: Wilson Gulch Trestle (D&RGW Farmington Branch)
spots.location: Wilson Gulch south of Durango on the former Farmington Branch right-of-way (county-owned strip)
spots.condition: Century-old wooden trestle (c.1905) still standing; branch abandoned 1968, rails removed by 1971.
spots.access: public (La Plata County-owned ROW)

verify.security_notes: Durango Herald says the right-of-way stayed in county hands. No current condition or security report found.

spots.name: Devil's Creek Railroad Trestle
spots.location: Silver Thread Scenic Byway (SH 149) stop #21, near Lake Fork canyon, Lake City, Hinsdale County
spots.condition: Railroad bed and trestle remains of the abandoned D&RG branch still at the site; timbers partly removed after abandonment.
spots.access: unknown (viewable from byway)

verify.security_notes: The byway's stop #21 page says trains stopped in 1933 and the trestle was taken apart two years later, with its timber moved to Gunnison. Only the site and grade remain as a byway stop. No security info.

spots.name: Gold Camp Road Tunnel 3 (Short Line railroad)
spots.location: Upper Gold Camp Road, closed 8.5-mi section on the former Colorado Springs & Cripple Creek District 'Short Line' grade
spots.condition: Former railroad tunnel partially collapsed 1988; road section closed to vehicles since; fire damage reported 2006; other tunnels on the grade remain. Open to hikers/bikers.
spots.access: public land (Pike National Forest / city)

verify.security_notes: 8.5-mile segment closed to vehicles since the 1988 partial collapse. A Feb 2006 fire destroyed the tunnel's timbers. The reopening plan was reversed on appeal and never funded. No post-2007 news found.

spots.name: Tennessee Pass railroad tunnels (original 1890 bore)
spots.location: Tennessee Pass on the dormant D&RGW/UP Tennessee Pass line beside US 24; 1945 tunnel 50 ft west of original; Belden Tunnel near Gilman, Leadville / Red Cliff, Lake-Eagle County
spots.condition: Line silent since 1997; original 1890 tunnel portals buried, part collapsed 2012 causing a highway sinkhole and was sealed; 1945 tunnel stands with snow curtain. Reddit exploration post May 2025.
spots.access: private (railroad property, line out of service)

verify.security_notes: Railroad property: the line is out of service but not abandoned (Gazette 2025). Colorado Midland & Pacific says trespassing on the line is illegal and asks people to report trespassers to police. An old tunnel collapse caused a 2012 US 24 sinkhole, which CDOT repaired. The Belden area near Gilman is subject to sheriff trespass citations.

spots.name: Uintah Railway grade and trestle sites, Baxter Pass
spots.location: Baxter Pass road north of Mack, which largely follows the old Uintah track bed; grade visible north of old US 6 west of Mack, Mack / Atchee, Garfield-Mesa County
spots.condition: Narrow-gauge line abandoned 1939; grade and several old trestle sites still visible; part of company hotel at Mack reportedly survives (unverified). Some sites on private property.
spots.access: mixed public (BLM road) / private

verify.security_notes: Grade still visible; a tour guide notes some sites are on private property. Baxter Pass is sometimes impassable in winter.

spots.name: Valley Drive-In
spots.location: On US Highway 34, Fort Morgan. Single screen, room for about 300 cars
spots.condition: Drive-ins.com says the theater is closed but the physical facility remains. The Fort Morgan Times reported in May 2011 that it would not reopen because of financial pressures. RoadArch says it closed in 2011 and the sign remains. Newest info is the undated drive-ins.com listing (site updated 2026).
spots.access: Private. The owner reportedly planned to lease the property (2011).

verify.security_notes: Closed in 2011. Drive-ins.com says the physical facility and sign remain. No security information found.

spots.name: Cave of the Winds abandoned exit road and farewell sign
spots.location: The former exit road of the Cave of the Winds attraction in Williams Canyon, about 3 miles up to Rampart Range Road, Manitou Springs, El Paso County
spots.condition: The road is abandoned and full of rockfall, with a stream running over it. The old sign bidding visitors farewell still stands. Graffiti reported as recent as 2018.
spots.access: Posted no trespassing, hiking or camping. A trail guide says it can be hiked if you have turned in a waiver at the Cave.

verify.security_notes: Privately owned. Posted signs prohibit hiking, camping and trespassing, and news pieces warn of prosecution. Trail guides say hiking is allowed only with a waiver signed at Cave of the Winds. A 2024 review says it is closed to vehicles.

spots.name: Former Russell Stover candy plant
spots.location: 2200 Stover Ave., Montrose (about 280,000 sq ft building on a 21.7-acre site)
spots.condition: Russell Stover closed the plant in 2020. It has been vacant since then. A planned 2021 food-processing reuse never happened, and a 2024 foreclosure auction drew no bidders. Local group Red Nile LLC bought it in 2024, and later local coverage says it is still vacant with no clear plans. Newest info: 2024.
spots.access: Private property, owned by Red Nile LLC since 2024

verify.security_notes: July 2024: Red Nile LLC bought the foreclosed plant for $4.5M and planned food processing and cold storage. No 2025-26 status or security info found.

spots.name: Ute-Ulay Mill and Town Site
spots.location: County Road 20 along Henson Creek, about 4 miles west of Lake City
spots.condition: Colorado Preservation Inc. put it on its Most Endangered Places list in 2015, naming the threat as 'demolition by neglect – vacant'. Denver7 calls it a decaying, neglected mining town. A 2011 blog called the mill 'remarkably intact', and a 2012 photo caption says the mill and some buildings are still standing. A Mining History Association tour describes a restored headframe and hoist house, a boarding house and a log cabin. It was listed on the National Register in 2017. Newest info: 2017.
spots.access: Interpretive site that visitors can tour (per Denver7 and the Mining History Association). Exact ownership unknown.

verify.security_notes: Abandoned mine openings were permanently closed and the headframe stabilized in fall 2012. Site is being reclaimed for heritage tourism, with partners including LKA Gold and Hinsdale County. Guided walks are led by a caretaker (video about a year old).

spots.name: Ohio City
spots.location: Ohio City townsite, northeast of Gunnison on the road toward Pitkin
spots.condition: Described as 'pretty much just a ghost town' apart from a few year-round residents. Original buildings still standing include the schoolhouse, jail and city hall, plus some cabins and old homes. Info is from tourism pages, year not stated.
spots.access: Unknown. Some residents live there, so treat buildings as private.

verify.security_notes: Semi-ghost town with some current residents. Its last business closed in 2016. Property has been advertised for sale (listing undated). No security info.

spots.name: Former Schmitt Elementary School
spots.location: 1820 S. Vallejo St., Denver
spots.condition: Closed in spring 2025 because enrollment fell. In 2026 it was still one of several vacant DPS buildings with no assigned use. DPS asked for reuse proposals in early 2026 (due March 2026), and Rocky Mountain Prep asked to put a campus there. No final decision had been reported as of spring 2026.
spots.access: Owned by Denver Public Schools; vacant district property

verify.security_notes: In March 2026 DPS was still vetting reuse ideas. No security reports found.

spots.name: Former Columbian Elementary School
spots.location: 2925 W. 40th Ave., Denver, CO 80211 (Sunnyside, northwest Denver; near 41st Ave. and Federal Blvd.)
spots.condition: Permanently closed in spring 2025 (38% utilization). It was one of five standalone DPS buildings left vacant in summer 2025. As of March 2026, DPS had issued a request for proposals and wanted it to become an infant and toddler child care center. Rocky Mountain Prep also asked for it. No final reuse had been reported in 2026.
spots.access: Owned by Denver Public Schools; vacant district property

verify.security_notes: DPS issued a reuse RFP in Feb 2026, and an early-learning-center proposal fell through. No security reports found.

spots.name: Former Moore Middle School
spots.location: 8455 W. 88th Ave., Westminster (about 13 acres)
spots.condition: Opened in 1980 and closed in 2024 when it merged with Pomona High. In 2025 it was one of 13 closed Jeffco schools still unsold, at about $150,000 a year in upkeep each. The city of Westminster sent Jeffco a nonbinding letter of intent to buy it. The city says the building is at the end of its useful life and contains asbestos and mercury, and that any public use would start with demolition, possibly for a fire station.
spots.access: Owned by Jeffco Public Schools; city of Westminster in purchase talks

verify.security_notes: Jeffco's Sept 2026 update says Westminster entered the municipal-interest process to acquire it. No sale finalized and no security reports found.

spots.name: Barth Hotel
spots.location: 1514 17th St., Denver (LoDo)
spots.condition: A 142-year-old landmark, built as a warehouse and turned into a hotel in the 1880s. It ran as assisted living for more than 40 years until Senior Housing Options moved all residents out by January 2025. It has sat vacant and listed for $2.5M since; BusinessDen calls it 'derelict.' In January 2026 the Downtown Development Authority granted $6M toward a senior housing conversion. Eaton Senior Communities was under contract with a year-end 2026 deadline to buy. No reports said renovation had started.
spots.access: Owned by Senior Housing Options (sale pending to Eaton Senior Communities / Urban Ventures)

verify.security_notes: Vacant since early 2025. In 2026 Eaton Senior Communities is under contract to buy it by year-end 2026. Construction is planned for spring 2027. No security reports found.

spots.name: Former Kullerstrand Elementary School
spots.location: 12225 W. 38th Ave., Wheat Ridge
spots.condition: Closed in May 2023. Wheat Ridge described it as a vacant Jeffco-owned school when it sought redevelopment or reuse partners. In 2025-26 it was still waiting for the city to pick a buyer. The closure is older than 24 months, but recent reports still describe it as vacant.
spots.access: Owned by Jeffco Public Schools; city of Wheat Ridge has first right to buy

verify.security_notes: Wheat Ridge sought reuse partners with responses due May 18, 2026. It appears in Jeffco's Sept 2026 disposition update. No buyer named and no security reports found.

spots.name: Former Wilmore Davis Elementary School
spots.location: 7975 W. 41st Ave., Wheat Ridge
spots.condition: Closed in May 2023 and still a vacant Jeffco property in recent reports. Wheat Ridge's council chose Spectra Centers, a school for children with disabilities, as its preferred buyer on June 22. spots.access: Owned by Mesa County Valley School District 51. Assume no public access.

spots.name: West Springs Hospital (former Mind Springs Health psychiatric hospital)

spots.access: Owned by Mind Springs Health, which says it is committed to maintaining the building. Assume private with no access.

spots.name: Leadville abandoned silver mine structures

spots.name: Former Stay Inn (city-owned motel, I-70 & Peoria)
spots.location: 12033 E. 38th Ave., near I-70 and Peoria St., Denver, Denver County
spots.condition: Four-story, 96-room former Stay Inn. Denver bought it in 2023 for $9M as homeless housing and boarded it up. It was still fenced off and had housed no one in 2025 reports. spots.name: Rossonian Hotel

spots.condition: Historic jazz-era hotel that Westword describes as still empty despite more than $3M in city loans and grants over three decades. Revival attempts, including one in 2005, failed. spots.name: Brandon ghost town: brick bank and abandoned houses

verify.security_notes: Nov 2019 blog: red brick bank 'dangerously close to collapsing'; vault visible. Population 21 (2020 census). No security info.

spots.name: Hotel Holly–Haswell Hotel
