spots.condition: Has sat vacant for years with the roof caved in; the city calls it an eyesore. Pueblo City Council approved a Circle K deal on Nov. 10, 2025 that calls for demolishing it. No source confirms it has been demolished yet, so it may be gone by now.
spots.access: Privately owned; slated for demolition

verify.security_notes: Vacant since 2018. On Nov 10, 2025 Pueblo council narrowly approved a Circle K and housing deal that requires demolition. A report cites a demolition vote in April 2026. Completed demolition was not confirmed. Active demolition or construction site likely.

spots.name: Abandoned motel at 1420 S. Nevada Ave
spots.location: 1420 S. Nevada Ave, between Arvada St and Brookside St, near downtown, Colorado Springs, El Paso County
spots.condition: Reported as an abandoned motel/hotel when it burned on May 19, 2024. Smoke was pouring out, flames came through the roof, and crews were warned of possible asbestos. Sources do not say whether it has been demolished since. Newest info: 2024.
spots.access: unknown; owner not named in sources

verify.security_notes: May 19, 2024 fire, with flames through the roof and possible asbestos. No information found after the fire.

spots.name: Former Elvis Cinemas Kipling 6 (Kipling Plaza 6)
spots.location: 6014 S. Kipling Parkway, Littleton
spots.condition: Closed since Feb 26, 2023. In Oct 2025 the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office asked for help identifying 'urban explorers' who broke in, blaming social media challenges. Interior condition unknown; 2026 status not confirmed.
spots.access: Private, closed building. The sheriff is actively pursuing intruders, so trespass risk is high.

verify.security_notes: Oct 2025: the Jefferson County Sheriff released surveillance video of 'urban explorers' forcing the front doors and sought to identify them, calling it a 'felony-level mistake.' The building is leased by a local church.

spots.name: Mesa Road abandoned houses with tunnels
spots.location: 1065 Mesa Road, 80904, Colorado Springs, El Paso County
spots.condition: A radio-station article built on a videographer's walkthrough video describes two boarded-up houses still standing, plus tunnels; possibly about 60 years abandoned. The tie to General Palmer is legend.
spots.access: Private property; the article warns of injury and trespassing prosecution.

verify.security_notes: Radio-station articles (undated) based on one explorer's video describe two boarded-up houses on private property and warn of trespassing prosecution. No official records found.

spots.name: Lucas Homestead ruins
spots.location: Castlewood Canyon State Park, Franktown, Douglas County
spots.condition: Abandoned concrete homestead ruins featured by explorer Derelict Doug ('American Ruins - The Lucas Homestead Discovered').
spots.access: Inside Castlewood Canyon State Park; legal to visit during park hours (park fee).

verify.security_notes: Interpreted historic site on a self-guided trail in Castlewood Canyon State Park. Needs a park pass and is open during park hours.

spots.name: Burke Springs Creek Ranch (abandoned farm and homestead)
spots.location: Old Park, off the Gore Pass road (CO-134 area), Toponas, Routt County
spots.condition: Derelict Doug post 'Abandoned Farm and Homestead - Old Park Colorado' shows a ranch falling into ruin. County not confirmed (Routt or Grand).
spots.access: Conservation easement land; treat as private.

spots.name: Lulu City ghost town
spots.location: Kawuneeche Valley, Rocky Mountain National Park. Colorado River Trailhead on US 34, about 9.5 mi north of the Kawuneeche Visitor Center. About 6.2 mi round trip on the Colorado River Trail, Grand Lake, Grand County
spots.condition: Silver camp from 1879 to about 1885. Reports differ: 3 recognizable cabin ruins out of 9, or one crumbling cabin plus building platforms and foundations. Old mine shafts nearby. On the National Register since 1977
spots.access: National Park Service (Rocky Mountain NP). Easy hiking trail, best June to October. A park entry pass is required

verify.security_notes: National park rules: do not remove artifacts or climb on ruins. Stay away from old mine shafts. Snow from about October to June

spots.name: Dutchtown ghost town
spots.location: Never Summer Mountains near timberline, above Lulu City. Reached by a side route near the Lake of the Clouds Trail, with the Dutch Town backcountry campsite nearby, Grand Lake, Grand County
spots.condition: Camp from about 1879 to 1884. The NPS nomination describes 4 decaying cabin ruins; one other source counts 3
spots.access: National Park Service (Rocky Mountain NP). Long, strenuous hike past Lulu City. Summer only

verify.security_notes: Free to visit with park entry. Overnight camping needs a backcountry permit. Remote high-altitude terrain: plan for lightning and getting lost

spots.name: Masontown ghost town (Victoria Mine)
spots.location: Mount Royal/Masontown Trail #1 on the east face of Mount Royal. Trailhead at the west end of Frisco (I-70 Exit 201, Frisco Main Street). About 1 mile of climbing
spots.condition: Founded in 1866. Destroyed by an avalanche around 1926 and fires through 1968. Foundations, scrap metal, collapsed cabin remains and mining equipment are still visible
spots.access: White River National Forest, Dillon Ranger District. Hiking trail, summer and fall. The Frisco Historic Park & Museum runs guided hikes

verify.security_notes: Steep trail. Do not take artifacts (federal law). This is avalanche terrain in winter

spots.name: Pieplant mill and cabins
spots.location: Pieplant Creek 4WD road (signed FR 742.3D in 2015) off County Road 742, north of Taylor Park Reservoir, Taylor Park / Almont, Gunnison County
spots.condition: Camp abandoned soon after 1910. A few log cabins remain; the Forest Service re-roofed one in 2006. Part of the 200-ton mill stands among collapsed mill and mine ruins
spots.access: Gunnison National Forest (GMUG). Rocky 4WD or hiking road. Snow-free roughly June to October. Dispersed camping nearby

verify.security_notes: Collapsed mill: do not enter or climb it. Watch for fire restrictions

spots.name: Vicksburg mining camp
spots.location: County Road 390 (Clear Creek Road), about 9-10 mi west of US 24 near Clear Creek Reservoir. The road continues to Winfield, Granite / Buena Vista, Chaffee County
spots.condition: About 7-10 original log cabins are still standing, and the cabin nearest the road is a museum run by the Clear Creek Canyon Historical Society. On the National Register
spots.access: Pike & San Isabel National Forest land, but many cabins are privately owned. Graded dirt road OK for cars in summer. The museum opens on some summer weekends

verify.security_notes: PRIVATE CABINS: view from the road and the museum only. Do not enter buildings. No services

spots.name: Sallie Barber Mine
spots.location: Sallie Barber Road. Lincoln Townsite Trailhead on French Gulch Road (about 3882 French Gulch Rd), or the V3 Trail from the B&B Trailhead, Breckenridge, Summit County
spots.condition: Mine worked from the 1880s to the 1940s. Breckenridge History stabilized the headframe and ore bin, and a grate covers the shaft. Interpretive signs
spots.access: Town of Breckenridge / Summit County open space. Old road closed to motor vehicles. Hike, bike or snowshoe year-round

verify.security_notes: Stay out of any open shafts. Do not climb the headframe

spots.name: Jessie Mill and Extension Mill (Gold Run Loop)
spots.location: Gold Run Road / Gold Run Loop in the Golden Horseshoe area northeast of Breckenridge. About a 3-mile round-trip hike
spots.condition: Partial remains of the 1890s Jessie Mill have been stabilized under a new roof that copies the historic roofline. The smaller Extension Mill is nearby. Caverns, tunnels and collapsed adits are visible on the hillside
spots.access: Golden Horseshoe open space trails (Breckenridge History trail guide). Hike or bike in summer. Guided snowshoe tours in winter

verify.security_notes: Sources warn that many sites are badly decayed: never enter or climb on ruins. Stay out of adits and caverns

spots.name: Mayflower tram towers, Arrastra Gulch
spots.location: Arrastra Gulch road off CO 110 (Animas River road) east of Silverton, climbing to the Mayflower Mine site
spots.condition: Many towers of the 10,100-ft Mayflower tram (the only steel-tower tram in the county) still stand along the road. The 1929-1991 Mayflower Mill below is owned by the San Juan County Historical Society
spots.access: BLM Tres Rios Field Office with San Juan County. Graded road; the top section is steep and loose (high clearance or 4WD). Summer and fall

verify.security_notes: See the mill only on historical society tours. Stay off tram towers and out of adits. Patented (private) claims are mixed in

spots.name: Grizzly Bear Mine ruins (Bear Creek National Recreation Trail)
spots.location: Bear Creek National Recreation Trail, trailhead at the US 550 tunnel south of Ouray. Ruins along the trail
spots.condition: A wooden mine building stands among mine debris (described in a current hiking guide)
spots.access: Uncompahgre National Forest, Ouray Ranger District. Hiking trail with steep exposed switchbacks. Summer and fall

verify.security_notes: Exposed cliff trail, so it is not for beginners. Do not enter mine openings. Not verified beyond a search snippet

spots.name: Chief Ouray Mine and boarding house
spots.location: Trail above Ouray's Box Canyon area, Uncompahgre National Forest
spots.condition: Abandoned mine and boarding house (komoot listing)
spots.access: Uncompahgre National Forest. Steep hiking trail, summer

verify.security_notes: Only one listing found. Check the route with the Ouray Ranger District. Stay out of the building and the mine

spots.name: Fulford ghost town
spots.location: East Brush Creek Road (FR 415), about 17 mi southeast of Eagle, near Fulford Cave Campground. Old Fulford Stagecoach Trail toward Yeoman Park
spots.condition: Post office from 1892 to 1910. A few cabins and old buildings remain
spots.access: White River National Forest, Eagle-Holy Cross Ranger District. The last mile is rough and rocky. Seasonal road closure about November 23 to May 20

verify.security_notes: Lower Fulford is a private subdivision (some cabins are private), so view from public land only. Entering Fulford Cave needs a permit

spots.name: Rourke Ranch (Wineglass Ranch) National Historic Site
spots.location: Picket Wire Canyonlands, Comanche National Grassland. About 8.5 to 8.8 miles one way along the Picket Wire Canyon Trail from the Withers Canyon Trailhead (about 17 miles round trip), past the dinosaur tracksite, La Junta, Otero County
spots.condition: Adobe and jacal buildings of a cattle and horse ranch that Eugene Rourke founded in 1871 and that ran until 1971. Listed on the National Register and preserved as a National Historic Site (USFS, checked 2026)
spots.access: US Forest Service, Comanche National Grassland. On foot, by bike or by horse; the only motorized access is the guided auto tour. Open all year, daylight only. Guided tours run on some Saturdays in May, June, September and October and need a reservation

verify.security_notes: Day use only; no overnight camping anywhere in the Picket Wire Canyonlands (USFS 2026). Long hike with no shade and extreme summer heat; carry at least 1 gallon of water per person. There are restrooms at the ranch. Do not disturb the adobe structures

spots.name: Dolores Mission and Cemetery ruins
spots.location: Picket Wire Canyon Trail, a few miles below the Withers Canyon Trailhead (about a 250 ft descent into the canyon). It is on the 11.2-mile round-trip route to the dinosaur tracks, La Junta, Las Animas County
spots.condition: Ruins of the adobe chapel of an 1870s Hispanic settlement of about 11 families, with a small cemetery of fragile carved headstones, some from the 1890s (sources seen 2026)
spots.access: US Forest Service, Comanche National Grassland. Hike or bike from the Withers Canyon Trailhead; the guided auto tour is the only motorized access. Daytime only, all year

verify.security_notes: Daytime use only and no camping (USFS 2026). Headstones are fragile, so do not touch them or make rubbings. Carry 1 gallon of water per person; it gets very hot

spots.name: Lopez Family Homestead adobe ruins
spots.location: Purgatoire River bottom in Picket Wire Canyon, Comanche National Grassland, south of La Junta. The exact point on the trail is not given in the sources
spots.condition: Decaying adobe walls of the Demacio and Loretta Lopez homestead, lived in from the late 1870s to 1903. UCCS students excavated it in 2003, and the Forest Service planned to stabilize it and interpret it for visitors
spots.access: US Forest Service, Comanche National Grassland, through Picket Wire Canyon (Withers Canyon Trailhead). Daylight only

verify.security_notes: This is an archaeological site: look only, and do not dig or remove anything (federal law). Exact location and current interpretation status not confirmed, so ask the Comanche NG office in La Junta. Same day-use and no-camping rules as the rest of the canyonlands (2026)

spots.name: Westbrook Homestead and Barlow & Sanderson stage station ruins, Vogel Canyon
spots.location: Vogel Canyon Picnic Area and trails, about 17 miles south of La Junta (off CO 109), Comanche National Grassland, Timpas area
spots.condition: Stone walls and a fireplace of the Westbrook homestead (Depression era) are still standing, along with ruins of an 1870s Barlow & Sanderson stage station and pieces of the old stage road. The site is part of a 500-acre archaeological district (USFS/recreation.gov, checked 2026)
spots.access: US Forest Service, Comanche National Grassland. Gravel road to the picnic area trailhead, then a short loop hike. Open all year

verify.security_notes: The archaeological district has rock art: do not touch it or collect anything. Report vandalism to the Comanche NG office in La Junta. Bring water, and watch for heat and rattlesnakes. The stage-station identification comes partly from a 2025 blog

spots.name: Picture Canyon homestead remains
spots.location: Picture Canyon, Carrizo Unit, Comanche National Grassland. Canyon Trail (1.75 mi round trip) and Mesa Trail (2.25 mi round trip) from the parking area; the longer Homestead loop is 8.5 mi round trip, Campo / Springfield, Baca County
spots.condition: The Forest Service describes early 20th-century homestead remains and stone ruins along the trails, near Crack Cave (USFS, checked 2026)
spots.access: US Forest Service, Comanche National Grassland, by gravel roads from US 287/160. Trails open all year. Crack Cave is sealed except for guided equinox tours in March and September

verify.security_notes: Per USFS, no camping in Picture Canyon and the spring water is not safe to drink (2026). Do not enter Crack Cave outside guided tours. Very remote; bring water and fuel

spots.name: Rambo Homestead cabin, Little Dominguez Canyon
spots.location: Dominguez Canyon Wilderness (Dominguez-Escalante NCA). From the Bridgeport Trailhead, hike about 2.5 mi to the Big/Little Dominguez confluence, then about 1 mile up Little Dominguez Canyon (3.5 to 4 mi from the trailhead), Whitewater / Delta, Mesa County
spots.condition: A one-room cabin from a 1911 Rambo family homestead, with skeletal 1920s-30s farm equipment, still standing (2021 article). Bill Rambo lived there until 2015, and the BLM acquired the land in 1988
spots.access: BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Dominguez-Escalante NCA. Foot or horse only; no bikes or mechanized equipment in the wilderness. Open all year

verify.security_notes: Wilderness rules apply. One source says overnight stays are restricted in the first few miles; check BLM camping rules (2026). Summer heat, no shade. The Bridgeport trailhead route crosses the railroad on a footbridge, and the route requires crossing creeks

spots.name: Skinner Cabin
spots.location: McInnis Canyons NCA, Fruita Paleo Area / Devils Canyon area. Reached by a short foot-only loop (about 1.8 mi) or from the Devils Canyon Trailhead (the Devils Canyon trail is 6.7 mi round trip)
spots.condition: Historic homestead cabin (one photo essay dates it to 1909). The BLM, HistoriCorps and partners restored it in 2016. One user report calls it old and unmaintained
spots.access: BLM Grand Junction Field Office, McInnis Canyons NCA. Foot-only trail. Open all year, no fee noted

verify.security_notes: Foot travel only. Do not collect fossils in the Paleo Area (federal law). Desert heat in summer. Current condition reports conflict (2016 restoration vs. 'unmaintained')

spots.name: Hanging Flume (Montrose Placer Mining Co. flume)
spots.location: Hanging Flume Overlook and interpretive site on CO 141 (Unaweep-Tabeguache Byway) above the Dolores River canyon, between Uravan and Gateway, Uravan / Naturita, Montrose County
spots.condition: Sections of an 1888-1891 wooden flume still hang on the cliff face halfway up the canyon wall. A 48-ft section was restored in 2012. It is on the National Register (1980) and the World Monuments Watch (2006)
spots.access: BLM Uncompahgre (Montrose) Field Office. Roadside overlook off CO 141 with interpretive signs. Open all year, free

verify.security_notes: View from the overlook only. The flume is on a sheer cliff and climbing to it is dangerous and damages a fragile National Register structure (2026)

spots.name: Captain Henry A. Smith's Cabin
spots.location: Escalante Canyon Road (from US 50 west of Delta), about 7.9 mi up the canyon, on the Escalante State Wildlife Area (Cap Smith Tract) in the Dominguez-Escalante NCA
spots.condition: Two cabins from 1911. The main one is built against a sandstone slab, with carved niches and a rock shelf bed. There is vandalism and deterioration; volunteers cleaned up and secured it in 2017
spots.access: Colorado Parks and Wildlife (Escalante SWA, Cap Smith Tract), with BLM land around it. Mostly dirt road with narrow shelf sections; the cabin is right off the road

verify.security_notes: Everyone 16 or older needs a valid hunting or fishing license or a State Wildlife Area pass on SWA land (CPW 2026). Much of the canyon floor below the cabin is private ranch land, so stay on the road. Colorado Preservation lists the site as endangered (2013) because of vandalism

spots.name: Walker Stone Cabin
spots.location: Escalante Canyon Road, Escalante Canyon (Dominguez-Escalante NCA area), west of Delta
spots.condition: A stone cottage of about 30 x 27 ft with mason-built walls, built in 1911 by homesteader Harry Walker and his sons. It has been badly vandalized; a 2018 State Historical Fund grant paid for repairs (due to finish in 2022)
spots.access: A blog reports it is state-owned and that visitors can go inside. Reached by the dirt Escalante Canyon Road

verify.security_notes: Ownership is reported as state-owned (blog) but not officially confirmed, so check with CPW or the BLM Uncompahgre FO. If it is on the Escalante SWA, an SWA pass or license is needed (2026). Private ranch land is nearby

spots.name: Two Bar Ranch ruins and Lodore School
spots.location: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge off CO 318. An easy 1.75-mi loop starts at the Lodore School, passes the Two Bar Ranch ruins and comes back along the Green River, Maybell, Moffat County
spots.condition: Ruined headquarters of the Two Bar Ranch (c. 1887-1895): main house, bunkhouse, log dugouts and other log buildings (NRHP 78000873). The 1910-11 Lodore School still stands; classes ran 1911-1947 (NRHP 1975)
spots.access: US Fish & Wildlife Service, Browns Park NWR. Reached via CO 318; hiking is allowed throughout the refuge

verify.security_notes: Wildlife-refuge rules apply, so check FWS for seasonal closures. Do not enter or climb on the log ruins. This is very remote far-northwest Colorado (2026)

spots.name: Crags Hotel ruins
spots.location: Rattlesnake Gulch Trail, Eldorado Canyon State Park. Start at the west Fowler Trail trailhead, about 0.5 mi into the canyon. The ruins are about 1.4 mi up, roughly 600 ft above the trailhead, on a grassy side path off the main trail., Eldorado Springs, Boulder County
spots.condition: Small brick ruins, foundations and remnants of a hotel built in 1908 that burned in 1912, after about four years in business. Benches with canyon views (sources seen 2015-2026).
spots.access: Colorado Parks & Wildlife. A state park pass is required. About 3.6 mi round trip with the upper loop. The park gets very crowded and can fill completely on weekends.

verify.security_notes: The upper part of the loop is sometimes closed in spring and summer for raptor nesting. Stay on the trail.

spots.name: Castlewood Canyon Dam ruins
spots.location: Castlewood Canyon State Park. Reached by the Creek Bottom Trail or the Castlewood Canyon Ruins Loop (4.75 mi, moderate)., Franktown, Douglas County
spots.condition: Both sides of an 1890 stone dam still stand. The dam failed in a storm in 1933 and flooded Denver. The breach is now a grassy path.
spots.access: Colorado Parks & Wildlife. Day use only, with no camping. A state park pass is required.

verify.security_notes: Day-use park. Follow the park's posted hours and stay on the trails.

spots.name: Crest House ruins (Mount Blue Sky summit)
spots.location: Summit parking area at the end of the Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) road, Arapaho National Forest. A 135 ft trail continues to the 14,265 ft summit., Idaho Springs, Clear Creek County
spots.condition: Stone shell of a restaurant and gift shop that opened in 1941-42 and was destroyed by a propane fire or explosion on September 1, 1979. The Forest Service stabilized it as an observation platform starting in 1992.
spots.access: USDA Forest Service, Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forest. Driving in requires a timed-entry ticket from recreation.gov. The road is seasonal, and a 2026 listing said the summit would reopen, conditions allowing, on Memorial Day weekend 2026. Off-season the summit can only be reached on hiking trails.

verify.security_notes: Use the stabilized ruin only as the observation platform it is meant to be. This is extreme high altitude, and the road closes seasonally (2026).

spots.name: Lost Park Reservoir shafthouse and historic cabins (Goose Creek)
spots.location: Goose Creek Trail #612 from the Goose Creek Trailhead, Lost Creek Wilderness, Pike National Forest. The cabins are about 4.1 mi in, on a signed 'Historic Buildings' spur. The shafthouse is about 0.5 mi farther., Deckers / Sedalia area, Jefferson County
spots.condition: Two semi-intact cabins, other ruins and an old car at the camp. Old machinery at the shaft house from a failed attempt to dam Lost Creek underground (trip reports seen up to 2022).
spots.access: USDA Forest Service, Pike-San Isabel National Forest. A long day hike of about 8 to 9.7 mi round trip. Wilderness rules apply.

verify.security_notes: Wilderness area: leave the artifacts in place and stay out of shafts. Check Forest Service conditions before going.

spots.name: Frazer Barn and homestead ruins (Frazer Meadow)
spots.location: Frazer Meadow, Golden Gate Canyon State Park. Reached by the Horseshoe Trail, or by the Burro and Mule Deer trails from Golden Gate Canyon Road., Golden / Black Hawk area, Gilpin County
spots.condition: State Register-listed Frazer's Barn (5GL.700) and ruins of the Frazer homestead cabin. Remnants of an old bread truck lie in the meadow (2023 hike report).
spots.access: Colorado Parks & Wildlife. A state park pass is required, and sources disagree on the day fee.

verify.security_notes: Historic structure: look from outside and do not climb on it.

spots.name: Staunton historic cabin district
spots.location: Historic Cabin Trail and Chase Meadow Trail, Staunton State Park. The Staunton Cabin is 1/4 mi along the Historic Cabin Trail. A 'Building Ruin' is marked on the Scenic Loop., Pine, Jefferson / Park County
spots.condition: Brola, Blaine, Richardson and Staunton cabins. The 1918 Staunton homestead cabin is on the National Register. A separate building ruin is marked on the route map.
spots.access: Colorado Parks & Wildlife. A state park pass is required. The Historic Cabin Trail is foot-only, so bikes use the Staunton Ranch Trail. Guided history hikes are offered at times.

verify.security_notes: The cabins are under preservation. Do not enter unless on a guided tour.

spots.name: Heil Valley Ranch lime kiln
spots.location: Lime Kiln Spur off the Lichen Loop (1.3 mi), Heil Valley Ranch Open Space. Take the signed trails east of the Heil parking area, across the creek bridges., Lyons area, Boulder County
spots.condition: Sandstone kiln once used to fire limestone into lime.
spots.access: Boulder County Parks & Open Space. The Lichen Loop is foot traffic only. No fee was mentioned in the sources.

verify.security_notes: Stay on the trail and do not climb the kiln.

spots.name: Woods Quarry and Roosa Cabin
spots.location: Junction of the Mesa Trail and the Woods Quarry Trail, near Chautauqua (City of Boulder OSMP). The quarry is a short spur uphill from the cabin.
spots.condition: Sandstone quarry used from the 1890s until it closed in the 1920s, with 'sandstone sofas' carved at the site. The small stone Roosa Cabin stands at the trail junction.
spots.access: City of Boulder Open Space & Mountain Parks. Free, with dogs on leash. Heavily used.

verify.security_notes: Check OSMP trail status before going.

spots.name: Old Kiln Trail lime kiln
spots.location: Old Kiln Trail and Old Kiln Spur, City of Boulder OSMP, off the Foothills South trail., Boulder (north), Boulder County
spots.condition: Remains of a crude lime kiln that may have made lime plaster and cement for the earliest CU buildings. The 2013 floods damaged the trail, and a narrow eroded section was still reported in 2015.
spots.access: City of Boulder Open Space & Mountain Parks. Free.

verify.security_notes: Check current OSMP status for flood damage. Stay on the trail.

spots.name: Cambria Lime Kiln
spots.location: East side of the Kinney Run Trail, Kinney Run Open Space / Eagle Ridge area (City of Golden).
spots.condition: Kiln built in 1879 by the Cambria Brick and Tile Co. and used until 1892. Its base was restored in 2009 and interpretive signs were added.
spots.access: City of Golden open space. A public trail, with no fee found in the sources.

verify.security_notes: Restored historic structure: do not climb it.

spots.name: North Table Mountain old quarries
spots.location: North Table Mountain Park. The Old Quarry Road is now part of the North Table Loop, and the West Quarry and Tilting Mesa trails pass the old quarries. West Trailhead: 4788 Hwy 93., Golden, Jefferson County
spots.condition: Two old basalt quarries on top of the mesa, now also used as climbing areas.
spots.access: Jefferson County Open Space. Free.

verify.security_notes: The Rim Rock Trail closes Feb 1 to Jul 31 each year for nesting birds. The quarry walls have steep drop-offs.

spots.name: Nelson House, Hall Ranch
spots.location: Nelson Loop Trail, Hall Ranch Open Space, reached from the Bitterbrush Trail (about 3.7 mi to the junction)., Lyons, Boulder County
spots.condition: The Nelson homestead house still stands, with a grain silo.
spots.access: Boulder County Parks & Open Space. Free.

verify.security_notes: View from the trail. Do not enter the house.

spots.name: Walker Ranch Homestead
spots.location: Walker Ranch Open Space, Flagstaff Road. The homestead complex is near the Walker Ranch Loop., Boulder (Flagstaff Rd), Boulder County
spots.condition: Ranch homesteaded in 1882 with original 1880s buildings, plus a newly reconstructed ranch house. National Register historic district (1984), which also includes sawmill and cyanide mill sites.
spots.access: Boulder County Parks & Open Space. The open space trails are free. The homestead itself is open to the public only for certain events, such as heritage days.

verify.security_notes: The homestead grounds are open only during scheduled events. Check the county calendar.

spots.name: White Ranch abandoned barn and ranch equipment
spots.location: Rawhide Trail, White Ranch Park. It is the first trail east of the West Trailhead (25373 Belcher Hill Rd). An open-air display of farm implements sits near a parking lot., Golden, Jefferson County
spots.condition: Abandoned ranch structures, a barn in a meadow, and old wagons and equipment from a cattle ranch the county bought in 1974.
spots.access: Jefferson County Open Space. Free, with about 20 mi of trails.

verify.security_notes: Leave the equipment in place. Check Jeffco for trail reroutes.

spots.name: Fourth of July Mine remnants
spots.location: Arapaho Pass Trail #904 from the Fourth of July Trailhead at the end of Fourth of July Road, at about 11,245 ft., Eldora / Nederland, Boulder County
spots.condition: Rusted machinery and leftover equipment at the inactive mine. The Forest Service has sealed the open shafts, including one 17 ft across.
spots.access: USDA Forest Service, Boulder Ranger District, Indian Peaks Wilderness edge. In winter the road closes at the west end of Eldora.

verify.security_notes: Stay away from mine openings. Seasonal road closure. Wilderness rules apply.

spots.name: Evans (Evans-Gandy) Homestead, Lincoln Mountain Open Space
spots.location: Homestead Trail, which branches off the Palmer Divide Trail about 1.25 mi from the Lincoln Mountain Open Space trailhead., Larkspur, Douglas County
spots.condition: National Register homestead, stabilized and preserved with about $400K. The trail and homestead had a ribbon-cutting on July 18, 2026.
spots.access: Douglas County Open Space. A public trail, with no fee mentioned in the sources.

verify.security_notes: Opened in July 2026. Confirm current access with Douglas County.

spots.name: Soderberg Homestead
spots.location: Soderberg Trailhead, Horsetooth Mountain Open Space, 1.2 mi along Shoreline Dr on the west side of the road. This is about 95 km from Denver, at the edge of the range., Fort Collins, Larimer County
spots.condition: Historic homestead and horse-ranch buildings, restored by HistoriCorps volunteers in September and October 2019.
spots.access: Larimer County Natural Resources. Open sunrise to sunset, and a park permit or fee is required.

verify.security_notes: Open sunrise to sunset. Do not enter the buildings.

spots.name: Hidden Valley lost ski area
spots.location: Hidden Valley, off Trail Ridge Road, Rocky Mountain National Park. Old lift lines (such as the Lower T-Bar) are still used as backcountry runs. About 100 km from Denver., Estes Park, Larimer County
spots.condition: The ski area ran until the NPS closed it in 1991 and removed its structures. Concrete lift footings, sign and snow-fence remnants, and lift-line scars remain (KUNC 2014). A sledding hill is still used.
spots.access: National Park Service. The park entrance fee applies.

verify.security_notes: There is avalanche terrain above treeline in winter. Leave the artifacts in place.

spots.name: Matterhorn Mill (Valley View Leasing and Mining Company Mill)
spots.location: About 2.8 miles south of Ophir, just off Colorado Highway 145, on the former Matterhorn townsite. A loop road connects it to the highway north and south of the mill. The mill is 96 ft tall and can be seen above the trees from the highway., Matterhorn townsite near Ophir, San Miguel County
spots.condition: Shut since 1968. Telluride News (2020) called it 'still remarkably intact' at its 100th anniversary. It is a 1920 flotation mill that was renovated in 1961 and listed on the NRHP in 2010. One low-quality page mentions restoration efforts. No status report after 2020 found.
spots.access: A 2009 record lists the owner as the U.S. Forest Service (Uncompahgre National Forest). Current access rules unknown.

spots.name: Atlantic Cable Mine headframe
spots.location: North side of Rico along Colorado Highway 145. A bronze marker sits on a mine car at the site.
spots.condition: Headframe built 1898-1905 and changed in the early 1940s. A mining record says the headframe was still standing in 1989. Marker photos from July 2025 show it still standing, with an exhibit beside it. Sources disagree on the hoist house: Waymarking says part of it survives, an art-photo page says it is gone.
spots.access: Unknown ownership. Waymarking says the site is fenced off, but it can be seen from the highway.

verify.security_notes: Fenced off, per Waymarking (date not given)

spots.name: Pandora Mill (Smuggler-Union / Idarado)
spots.location: Pandora townsite at the east end of the Telluride box canyon, on Idarado Mining Company land
spots.condition: Stopped processing ore in 1974 or 1978 (sources disagree). In 2016 the Telluride Historical Museum said the mill faced demolition. A 2017 state mining-agency letter discussed keeping the mill building and a few outbuildings for viewing from outside. Travel pages describe some structures still standing. No 2024-2026 status found, so it may have been demolished since.
spots.access: Private (Idarado Mining Company). Tailings are being reclaimed, and housing is expected on the site.

verify.security_notes: Active reclamation site owned by a mining company (2016-2017). No specific security details found.

spots.name: Feminilas Building (SPMDTU women's auxiliary hall)
spots.location: Culebra Valley, southeast of San Luis (Westword calls it El Rito; other sources say Culebra Valley), near San Francisco / San Luis, Costilla County
spots.condition: Crumbling adobe built about 1920. On Colorado's Most Endangered Places list in 2023 with the threat given as demolition by neglect. CPI's project status reads 'Progress', but I found no news of 2024–2025 stabilization work
spots.access: Owned by the SPMDTU / property owners; CPI said it would work with the owners on stabilization

spots.name: Boyd School (historic elementary school)
spots.location: Boyd School block, across the street from Boyd Park, Alamosa
spots.condition: Alamosa News describes the 34,000 sq ft school as sitting vacant. The SLV Housing Coalition bought it in late 2022 for an affordable-housing conversion. In 2025 the coalition was redesigning the plan ('Moose Manor'), and I found no confirmation that construction has started. Treat it as vacant but slated for redevelopment
spots.access: Owned by the San Luis Valley Housing Coalition

spots.name: Former Canon Potato packing shed
spots.location: 1016 E. State Highway 112, Center, CO (has a railroad spur)
spots.condition: A commercial listing (undated, seen 2026) describes it as vacant: more than 90,000 sq ft of warehouse, office and storage space, sold as real estate only
spots.access: Private; listed for sale

spots.name: Bonanza ghost town remnants (incl. Empire Chief Mill ruins)
spots.location: Townsite at about 9,500 ft. From Villa Grove go north on US 285, then left onto County Rd LL56 for about 14 miles. The Empire Chief Mill is near town, Bonanza, Saguache County
spots.condition: Largely abandoned former silver town. Sources say a few old houses, mine structures and rock piles remain; one says several historic buildings remain. The Empire Chief Mill is an avalanche-destroyed ruin, and an old ore mill is described as partly fallen down. 30 buildings burned in the 1937 fire. CPR reported the state was weighing declaring the town abandoned as a municipality. The Rawley Mill was reportedly dismantled in an ASARCO cleanup
spots.access: Mixed: the townsite is reached by county road; mine and mill parcels are likely private (a Rawley/Bonanza property was offered at auction)

verify.security_notes: Remote and rough road; a guide warns a standard sedan will likely suffer severe undercarriage damage. No guards or fencing reported

spots.name: Holy Moses Mine ruins
spots.location: About 3 miles up East Willow Creek from Creede, off the Bachelor Loop
spots.condition: SAH Archipedia says the Holy Moses ruins can still be seen. This was the 1889 strike that started Creede's silver rush. I found no source with a recent condition or date
spots.access: Sources say almost all of the Bachelor Loop runs through private land

verify.security_notes: Sources warn the mine buildings are structurally unsound and the shafts may hold poisonous or explosive gases; they advise staying off private property

spots.name: Artesia (Artesian) Motel
spots.location: 640 Highway 50, north side of the highway, Orchard Mesa, Grand Junction (Orchard Mesa), Mesa County
spots.condition: A local radio article (undated) calls it the 'old abandoned pink motel' and says the owners had recently applied for a fence permit. I found no newer status, so it may have changed.
spots.access: Privately owned; owners unknown

verify.security_notes: The owners applied to the city for a fence permit (article undated), so the site may now be fenced.

spots.name: Grand Junction Union Depot (1906 D&RG passenger depot)
spots.location: Downtown Grand Junction next to the current Amtrak station, at the south end of Main St/2nd St
spots.condition: Vacant for decades since Amtrak moved out in 1991, with deferred maintenance. In late 2025 it was still unoccupied but getting slow restoration: a $250k State Historical Fund grant (late 2025) for roof and utility stabilization, window restoration under way, and a federal grant bid in Nov 2025.
spots.access: Privately owned (Grand Junction Union Depot owners). An active restoration site, not open to the public.

verify.security_notes: Owners are present and restoration crews were active in 2024-2025.

spots.name: Vulcan Mine remnants (burning coal mine)
spots.location: South side of the Colorado River, about 2 miles from New Castle. Visible looking east up the river from Grand River Park.
spots.condition: Abandoned after the 1896 and 1913 explosions, and the coal seam is still burning underground. Mine remnants are visible from Grand River Park; the sources are undated.
spots.access: Private property. View only from Grand River Park or Burning Mountain Park (Coal Miner Memorial).

verify.security_notes: Underground coal fire: risk of toxic gas and ground collapse.

spots.name: Old Lutheran Medical Center campus (former Lutheran hospital, Lutheran Legacy Campus)
spots.location: Former hospital campus near W. 38th Avenue and N. Lutheran Parkway (about 100 acres; 92 acres sold), Wheat Ridge, Jefferson County
spots.condition: In August 2025 Wheat Ridge police reported a summer spike in break-ins at the empty former hospital building, which they linked to the online 'urban exploring' trend. The hospital moved to Clear Creek Crossing in August 2024. In Dec 2025 E5X Management bought the site for $60M and plans 1,000+ housing units. I found no demolition report as of the sources.
spots.access: Private (sold by Intermountain Health to developer E5X Management, Dec 2025); no public access

verify.security_notes: 2025: full-time security and a camera system used to identify suspects; police added graveyard-shift patrols; multiple arrests of adults and juveniles; police warned of possible felony charges and said parents were unaware their kids were doing this.

spots.name: William Penn Apartments
spots.location: 1644 Pennsylvania St., North Capitol Hill / Uptown, Denver, Denver County
spots.condition: A judge ordered the building closed in January 2025 because of deteriorating conditions: no heat, hot water or natural gas, and a fire alarm system that did not work. A later Townsquare feature (espnwesterncolorado/kekbfm, around 2026) says it remains closed a year later. It is on Denver's Neglected and Derelict Buildings list, with over $280,000 in fines and three liens.
spots.access: Private (owned by CBZ Management); closed by city/court order

verify.security_notes: 2025: closed under court order and city enforcement; a Denver judge issued an arrest warrant for the CBZ owner. No sources describe guards or fencing.

spots.name: Union Pacific Pumphouse
spots.location: Union Pacific rail line in Kit Carson (exact address not found)
spots.condition: Vacant. Listed 2005 for 'Demolition by Neglect – Vacant'. CPI status ALERT, and CPI made it one of five priority sites in 2022. Union Pacific has suggested moving it, which is not final. Thought to be Colorado's only surviving stone railroad pumphouse. No 2024-2025 condition report found.
spots.access: Owned by Union Pacific Railroad. Not open to the public.

verify.security_notes: No fencing or enforcement details found. Active railroad property, and railroads commonly prosecute trespass.

spots.name: Silver Dollar Saloon
spots.location: Downtown Victor National Register historic district (street address not found)
spots.condition: Boarded up since the 1950s. Listed 2008 for 'Demolition by Neglect – Vacant', CPI status IN PROGRESS (still under Progress in the 2014 CPI brochure). Bought by sympathetic owners in 2008, who got a State Historical Fund grant for a new roof and a structural assessment. Work later stalled because of health problems in the owners' family.
spots.access: Privately owned. Viewable from the street only.

verify.security_notes: Boarded up (CPI, undated). In a town center, so trespass would be noticed.

spots.name: Lewis Mill
spots.location: Bridal Veil Basin, about 12,450 ft, about 3.5 miles southeast of Telluride. Reached by hiking trail., near Telluride, San Miguel County
spots.condition: Intact but disused mill. Stabilized in 2001. Listed 1998 for demolition by neglect. CPI status Saved. On the National and State Registers since 2009. A feasibility study for a two-phase repair project exists (date unknown).
spots.access: Privately owned (CPI describes persuading 'the current owners'). Seen from the trail. Remote high-altitude site.

spots.name: Emma Store buildings
spots.location: Beside Highway 82 between Basalt and Willits, next to the Emma Trail and Rio Grande Trail
spots.condition: Unused for many decades. Structurally stabilized in recent years by Pitkin County Open Space and Trails with State Historical Fund money. A 2020-2021 county process recommended a future reuse. Listed 2000 (threat: neglect and highway vibration). CPI status Saved, with long-term preservation 'still unfolding'.
spots.access: Pitkin County Open Space and Trails bought the 12.5-acre townsite in 2008. The exterior can be seen from the public trails. On the county historic register with preservation covenants.

spots.name: Thomasville Lime Kilns
spots.location: Fryingpan River valley at Thomasville
spots.condition: Ruins that are still deteriorating, per Pitkin County officials. The county stabilized them starting in 2006 with CDOT money, earmarked $365,000 from its 2025 general fund for repairs, and approved a historic designation. Listed 2001 for demolition by neglect. CPI status Saved.
spots.access: Pitkin County manages the site and the ownership issues were resolved in 2004, but current title holder not confirmed. Listed on the Aspen Trailfinder site as a destination.

spots.name: Rock Creek Stage Stop (Rock Creek Stage Station)
spots.location: Rock Creek near Gore Pass, Routt National Forest
spots.condition: Stabilized and restored in 2000-2001 by the Forest Service, Historic Routt County and others. Not back in use: it was vacated in the 1940s and stands as a historic structure. Listed 2000 for 'Demolition by Neglect – Vacant'. CPI status Saved.
spots.access: On U.S. Forest Service land. Can be seen from public forest land.

verify.security_notes: No security reported. Remote forest site, but federal rules against damaging historic structures apply.

spots.name: McElmo Creek Flume (Flume No. 6)
spots.location: Off U.S. Highway 160 east of Cortez, at the McElmo Flume Overlook pullout
spots.condition: Disused flume. Foundation rebuilt after a 2014 grant, overlook dedicated December 2016, and declared officially saved after restoration in 2018. Listed 2011. On the National Register.
spots.access: Public viewing from the highway pullout, walkway and overlook with information panels.

verify.security_notes: Meant to be viewed from the overlook, not entered (2016 to present).

spots.name: State Soldiers' and Sailors' Home historic buildings (Homelake)
spots.location: Colorado State Veterans Community Living Center at Homelake campus, Homelake (near Monte Vista), Rio Grande County
spots.condition: Some historic buildings not used by the Veterans Center are vacant and deteriorating. The Homelake Foundation is restoring the chapel and the Old Administration Building with a $182,036 State Historical Fund grant. Listed 2005 for 'Demolition by Neglect – Vacant'. CPI status IN PROGRESS.
spots.access: State-owned campus that still runs as a veterans care facility. The vacant buildings are not open.

verify.security_notes: Active state veterans care facility with staff and residents on site. Entering the vacant buildings without permission would be trespass on state property.

spots.name: Newman Block (Granada Fish Market / Newman's Drug Store)
spots.type: Historic commercial block (four buildings with shared walls)
spots.location: Downtown Granada, near the former Amache (Granada Relocation Center) site. Exact street address not verified.
spots.condition: Added to Colorado's Most Endangered Places in 2025 (new listings start at Alert). A shared wall between the buildings has collapsed. The Fish Market part (opened 1943 by a released Amache internee) is vacant. The Newman's Drug Store part (built before 1914) is used as a rental event space. No update found after 2025.
spots.access: Owner not identified in the sources. Part of the block is in active use as an event space. It is a downtown building, so view it from the public sidewalk only.

verify.security_notes: Collapsed wall reported in 2025, so the structure is unsafe.

spots.name: Iglesia de San Antonio / Tiffany Church
spots.location: Rural Tiffany community, La Plata County. Exact address not verified.
spots.condition: Listed in 2019; CPI status is Progress. The adobe and stucco exterior is crumbling but the interior is reported well preserved. A stabilization project has been under way since about 2020 with State Historical Fund involvement. No completion confirmed as of 2026. A 100-year Mass is planned for 2028. On the La Plata County Register.
spots.access: Ownership not confirmed (church or parish property). Not described as open to the public.

spots.name: Doyle Settlement (schoolhouse, ruins and cemetery)
spots.type: Ruined 1859 settlement: one standing schoolhouse, foundations, ruins and a cemetery
spots.location: Along Doyle Road on the Huerfano River, about 38°3′30″N 104°24′51″W., Southeast of Pueblo, Pueblo County
spots.condition: Listed in 2018. Lies in ruins: the schoolhouse is the only standing building, with some foundations and the cemetery remaining. Joseph Doyle's house (Casa Blanca) is gone. Also nominated to the National Trust's 11 Most Endangered list in 2020. On the National Register.
spots.access: Only one source (Colorado Preservation) says Pueblo County owns it. No source says it is open to visitors.

spots.name: Montoya Ranch
spots.type: Adobe Hispano ranch house (about 1860-1869) with a full adobe basement
spots.location: Montoya Ranch near Farisita (Huerfano River valley). Exact address not verified., Near Farisita, Huerfano County
spots.condition: Listed in 2014; CPI status is Alert. Threat listed as Demolition by Neglect. Still standing in 2014. Added to the National Register in 2012. No condition report found after 2014, and current occupancy is not confirmed.
spots.access: Privately owned: Taos art dealer James Gerken bought it in 2000 to save it from demolition.

spots.name: Isis Theatre (Victor)
spots.location: Downtown Victor historic district. Exact street address not verified.
spots.condition: Listed in 2020; CPI status is Alert. Threat listed as Neglect. Long closed. The City of Victor supports rehabilitation as part of its Main Street effort. No 2024-2026 progress confirmed. One undated comment mentions a new owner, but it may refer to a different Isis theater.
spots.access: Owner not confirmed. Closed to the public. It sits on Victor's main commercial streets, so view it from outside only.

spots.name: 4 Bar 4 Ranch (stagecoach station and hotel)
spots.type: 1895 stage stop and roadhouse hotel, plus barn
spots.location: Former Berthoud Pass stage route near Fraser. Exact address not verified., Near Fraser, Grand County
spots.condition: Listed in 2014. CPI now marks it Saved, but restoration is unfinished. The Ford Barn was restored after a 2018 State Historical Fund grant. The hotel still needs stabilization and exterior work: a 2024 grant application sought money to rebuild its windows and doors. Described as vacant since ranching ended in the late 1980s.
spots.access: Sources disagree on the owner: Historic Fraser Inc. (from 2016) or the Stagecoach Meadows HOA (2014 report). It is an active restoration site.

verify.security_notes: Active restoration site; 2024 grant application for window and door work.

spots.name: Former Zerger Elementary School
spots.location: 9050 Field St, Westminster, CO
spots.condition: Jeffco closed it as a neighborhood school in 2011 or 2012 (sources disagree). Charter schools leased it until 2023, and a closed-schools roundup listed it as vacant in 2025. No source says the sale has closed (2026).
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The board approved a sale to Cardel Homes in June 2024 for about 40 homes, at $45,000 per lot the city approves. The deal closes only after Westminster approves the lots, and one report says the council approved 40 homes. Neighbors pushed for a park instead.

spots.name: Former Allendale Elementary School
spots.location: Allendale neighborhood, Arvada (street address not confirmed)
spots.condition: Closed 2021 (vacant since June 2021 per district slides). Reported in 2025 as empty for about 6 years, costing the district about $150,000 a year to maintain. Redevelopment is pending and demolition is not confirmed (2026).
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owned it. Jeffco's COO said in a podcast that it went to Cardell Homes for purchase in 2024, for conversion to single-family homes. A nearby home listing mentions preliminary city approval for the new development. No source confirms the sale has closed; if it has, the owner is the developer.

spots.name: Former Peck Elementary School
spots.location: 6495 Carr St, Arvada, CO 80004
spots.condition: Closed summer 2023. As of the 2025 roundup the district had not yet considered it for surplus, meaning it might still need the building. It was not on the district's 2026 municipal-interest list.
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. No sale or reuse plan was announced in the sources found.

spots.name: Former Arvada K-8 School
spots.location: 5751 Balsam St, Arvada, CO 80002
spots.condition: Closed at the end of the 2023-24 school year. Still district-owned and in the municipal-interest process (2026).
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The district's property disposition page lists it in the municipal-interest process, which gives the City of Arvada first chance to buy. No deal was reported.

spots.name: Former Parr Elementary School
spots.location: 5800 W 84th Ave, Arvada, CO 80003
spots.condition: Closed 2023 and declared surplus in April 2024. Still in the municipal-interest process (2026).
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The City of Arvada expressed interest in 2024, and the district's disposition page lists it in the municipal-interest process. No sale was reported.

spots.name: Former Colorow Elementary School
spots.location: 6317 S Estes St, Littleton, CO 80123, Littleton (mailing address), Jefferson County
spots.condition: Closed 2023 and declared surplus on March 13, 2025. Listed in the municipal-interest process (2026). No buyer was reported.
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The district is offering it first to the city or county through the municipal-interest process.

spots.name: Former Bergen Meadow Elementary School
spots.location: Evergreen, CO. Sources conflict: one gives 1892 Bergen Pkwy, another says the school was built on Hiwan Dr., Evergreen (unincorporated), Jefferson County
spots.condition: Closed in May 2024 after 53 years, when students moved to the remodeled Bergen Valley campus. Declared surplus in March 2025. Listed in the municipal-interest process (2026).
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The district is in talks with Jefferson County, using a 'bundled approach', about whether the county wants the site.

spots.name: Former Molholm Elementary School
spots.location: 6000 W 9th Ave, Lakewood, CO 80214
spots.condition: Closed at the end of May 2023, when students went to Lumberg and Edgewater elementaries. The district said it was not on its list to sell. Current use has not been confirmed since about 2024.
spots.access: Jeffco Public Schools owns it. The nonprofit Edgewater Collective wants to buy it for a community center, but no deal was reported. Neighbors (Concerned Citizens for Molholm) want the green space kept.

spots.name: Former Remington Elementary School
spots.location: 4735 Pecos St, Denver, CO 80211
spots.condition: Denver Public Schools closed it as a district elementary in 2008. Its most recent tenant was a charter school, and Chalkbeat described it as vacant in 2026. As of July 2026 its future was still undecided.
spots.access: Denver Public Schools owns it and will only lease or partner, not sell. A 2026 request for proposals drew a pitch from soccer club Albion SC Denver for an indoor and outdoor sports complex, and the district was doing due diligence as of March to July 2026.
